title: WNBA launches search for next commissioner, but outgoing Cathy Engelbert could stay into 2027
description: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert says more than a dozen candidates are in the mix to succeed her, with officiating and player relations among top issues.
fullContent:
The WNBA's search for Cathy Engelbert’s successor has officially kicked off. According to reports, the league will work to eventually narrow down a list of more than a dozen candidates.

Engelbert’s eight-year, at-times tumultuous tenure is nearing its end, but she could remain in the role beyond 2026 if the search extends into 2027.

Engelbert previously announced plans to retire at the end of the year but clarified that she would remain commissioner beyond Dec. 31 if a successor was not in place. She took over as commissioner in 2019.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Monday marked Engelbert’s final WNBA Board of Governors meeting. Representatives from all 15 current teams attended, along with officials from the three expansion franchises set to join the league over the next four years: Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver also attended.

That meeting came a few days after Engelbert met with coaches, general managers and team presidents last week at the WNBA offices for the annual competition committee meetings.

If the WNBA chooses not to extend Engelbert’s tenure beyond Dec. 31, it could consider NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum. Tatum served as interim WNBA commissioner for nine months before Engelbert was hired following Lisa Borders’ departure in 2018.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS SHE'S TALKED WITH NBA COMMISSIONER ADAM SILVER AMID SEARCH FOR WNBA'S NEXT COMMISSIONER

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The next commissioner of the league will inherit a host of issues, including officiating, the transgender debate, scheduling and improving a strained relationship with players.

The league thrived in many ways during Engelbert’s tenure. Under her leadership, the WNBA enjoyed record growth and popularity, and signed a record-breaking broadcasting deal. Players surpassed $1 million in annual salaries.

WNBA EXPANDS REGULAR SEASON TO 50 GAMES STARTING IN 2027, THE LONGEST SCHEDULE IN LEAGUE HISTORY

But despite her accomplishments, Engelbert’s relationship with players was cordial at best, confrontational at other times. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart may have summed it up best when said players "respect" Engelbert.

Late last month, Engelbert presented the WNBA championship trophy to the Golden State Valkyries after they defeated the Atlanta Dream in the league’s first Finals series to reach seven games.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: This Is Why Vitalik Buterin Wants Crypto to Act More Like Housing
description: Buterin sees housing's limited liquidity as worth borrowing while warning crypto against incentives that keep homes expensive.
fullContent:
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has called for digital assets to adopt some of the long-term investment habits of the housing sector.

According to him, crypto platforms have made it much easier to trade than hold, and the question now is whether an asset class built around liquidity can develop a culture that rewards patience.

Buterin Wants Digital Assets to Borrow Housing’s Restraint

Buterin was responding to a Pew report about the housing situation in Raleigh, North Carolina, shared by the chief economist at the Center for Independent Studies, Peter Tulip. The report found that looser zoning rules had helped to bring down inflation-adjusted rents by 15% in the last three years, with low-income renters benefiting the most.

According to Buterin, when younger people put money into stocks and digital assets instead of into houses, it comes with one upside:

“It reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities.”

In his opinion, housing has an advantage as an investment, in that it is encouraged by both policy and mainstream culture as a “safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.”

However, newer platforms have been encouraging the complete opposite, which, as the Ethereum co-founder put, has led to “more irresponsible behavior.”

“We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets,” he wrote.

He didn’t propose any specific product or rule that could help crypto achieve the above; instead, he framed the challenge as one of investment culture, with the crypto industry needing to find ways to encourage people to hold their assets for longer periods without copying the sort of incentives that kept housing prices high.

ETH’s Store-of-Value Case Facing a Market Test

Buterin’s post has come about a week after he argued that ETH should be judged as a store of value and not for the transaction fees the network burns.

However, the token is currently facing a difficult stretch, with data from CoinGecko at the time of writing showing it down more than 12% across the last 7 days and 21% lower than where it was two weeks ago. It’s the same across longer timeframes, including a 25% plunge on the 30-day chart that has helped push ETH 40% down year-on-year.

The world’s second-largest cryptocurrency recently fell to around $1,700, its lowest level since July, amid selling by the Ethereum Foundation of 10,000 ETH for more than $19 million. Also, the token’s case hasn’t been helped by seven straight weeks of outflows for spot Ethereum ETFs, with this week already more than $45 million in the red.

title: CoinShares CEO Blames AI for Bitcoin’s Slide, but AI Stocks Are Falling Too
description:
CoinShares CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti says AI is draining crypto, yet Nvidia and the S&P 500 are also sliding this week.
The post CoinShares CEO Blames AI for Bitcoin’s Slide, but AI Stocks Are Falling Too appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
CoinShares CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti blames artificial intelligence for draining crypto liquidity. Bitcoin is down about 24% in a month, yet AI stocks are falling too.

Nvidia dropped 2.9% on Wednesday, and the S&P 500 logged a fifth straight loss. Crypto holders and AI shareholders are both absorbing losses.

Is the CoinShares CEO Right That AI Is Draining Crypto?

Mognetti leads CoinShares, a European digital asset manager. He told CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” this week that AI is absorbing capital once bound for digital assets.

“has been sucking out every single marginal dollar in the industry from crypto.”

Jean-Marie Mognetti, CoinShares CEO, speaking to CNBC

However, equities complicate that reading. Nvidia (NVDA) gave back early gains on Wednesday despite beating earnings estimates, according to CNBC.

Moreover, the S&P 500 slid 0.23%, its longest losing run since June. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42% after hitting its lowest level since April on Tuesday.

The pressure builds on a chip stock sell-off last week. A basket of 62 chip stocks lost more than $650 billion in two sessions.

Eric Parnell, chief market strategist at Great Valley Advisor Group, told CNBC the sector remains fragile.

“It doesn’t take much of a slowdown in earnings growth in the environment that we’re in with the AI buildout and the AI spend to take these types of stocks down pretty quickly.”

Eric Parnell, Great Valley Advisor Group, speaking to CNBC

Will Anthropic’s Debut Decide Which Story Holds?

Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) is set for this week. Sources told CNBC the shares are expected to price above the $70 to $78 range.

Mognetti said a strong debut would lift risk assets. In contrast, a weak one would raise doubts over AI financing and could revive crypto’s debasement narrative.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin traded near $62,300 on Thursday, according to Bitcoin price data. BeInCrypto’s SpaceX IPO pattern analysis found a 23% drop since Sept. 30, versus 19% before SpaceX’s June listing.

Mognetti cited a strong dollar and falling stablecoin liquidity. Parnell, however, flagged AI spending and debt financing. Both explanations could tie Bitcoin and AI shares to the same funding conditions.

Still, a strong debut that lifts AI shares while Bitcoin keeps falling would favor Mognetti’s rotation case.

The post CoinShares CEO Blames AI for Bitcoin’s Slide, but AI Stocks Are Falling Too appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Costco sees surge in panic buying after a string of tech outages, report says
description:
Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency-preparedness items in response to a recent string of technology outages, according to investment firm Mizuho Securities. 
"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report. 
Shoppers are "pantry-loading," while 21 of the retailer's 26 "high-ticket generators" were sold out online as of Sunday night, he added. 
The recent outages, which blocked access to Microsoft apps, snarled flights nationwide and hindered banking activities at various times during the past week, are raising questions among Americans about a larger cybersecurity threat, CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman said on "CBS Mornings" on Wednesday. 
The companies affected by the outages have said they were due to issues such as routine maintenance or upgrades, while the Federal Aviation Administration blamed its nationwide ground stop last week on a contractor updating its flight system.
"All of them have denied that cyberattacks are to blame," Gutman said. "Still, the system failures are fueling online speculation about a larger cyber threat."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that there's "zero evidence" that the recent outages in the U.S. are linked. 
"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said during a news conference in the Philippines. 
Costco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
The close timing of the outages highlights the country's increasing reliance on technology, John D'Arcy, a Temple University professor who researches cybersecurity and information technology failures, told CBS News Philadelphia.
"Our systems are so much more complex and so much more interconnected than they ever have been in the past, that when we just have one failure, the effects are much more dramatic," D'Arcy said.
The surge in panic buying could lift Costco's sales, Bellinger wrote. He raised his target price for the company's stock to $1,150 from $1,100. Other big-box stores, including Walmart and Sam's Club, could see similar "pantry-loading lifts," he added.
This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/costco-panic-buying-tech-outages-generators/

title: 'There was no monitoring': Sources dispute FAA oversight of work before ground stop
description:
Passengers wait at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), in Arlington, Virginia, just outside Washington, DC, on November 14. - Aaron Scwartz/AFP/Getty Images
On the morning of last week’s historic nationwide ground stop, an FAA technician escorted a private contractor from L3Harris into a remote radio communications site for air traffic control centers in south Arkansas, to replace a decades-old router.
The FAA technician believed his role ended when the contractor entered the facility. He went about his own work without knowing exactly what the L3Harris engineer was doing, according to two sources familiar with what happened in the room, and the union that represents FAA technicians.
Not long after it was replaced, that new router triggered a cascade of communications problems, flooding the FAA’s aging network with data and leading the FAA to take the rare step later that day of issuing a full nationwide ground stop. About 3,500 planes were in the air when departures were halted for more than four hours while the agency worked to figure out the problem.
The details of how that router was installed and who was overseeing that work is now in dispute and emerging as a key point of tension in unraveling what exactly went wrong that day.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford has defended the FAA’s modernization process and insisted that the L3Harris engineer performing the upgrade “was monitored by an FAA technician” and that a risk assessment was done beforehand.
But sources who spoke to CNN dispute this characterization. The technician “was only there to unlock the door,” one of them said.
“There was no monitoring,” another source said.
That kind of hands-off arrangement, sources say, is a recent development and represents a stark change from how this kind of maintenance work was handled by previous administrations, when the FAA typically exercised far more oversight of contractors’ work.
A crucial memo from March 2025
But in an effort to speed up and streamline the modernization of the nation’s air traffic control system with $12.5 billion from President Donald Trump’s “big beautiful bill,” the administration diminished FAA oversight of this kind of work, the sources said.
In a memo dated March 2025, the FAA laid out some key changes to how maintenance and upgrades would be carried out, noting: “It is critical to approve maintenance performed by the Telecommunication Vendors without delay.”
Under the policy change, the FAA shifted from receiving maintenance “requests” from its private contractors to receiving “notifications” of intended work, noting that “this work will proceed without FAA approval,” according to the memo.
Airplanes are parked on the tarmac after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop "due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety" following the agency's earlier report of serious air traffic control communications issues at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on November 13. - Jonathan Ernst/Reuters
The memo does note that an FAA liaison will evaluate the “purpose, severity, criticality and impact” of the work, but the sources told CNN there are only a handful of liaisons nationwide processing thousands of notifications.
“So what level of oversight are they really doing?” one of the sources said.
As a result, the L3Harris contractor at the center of Friday’s outage showed up with just a few days’ notice and conducted the work without any meaningful oversight from the agency, according to the sources and the union.
The March 2025 memo “laid the groundwork for what happened last Friday,” the source said.
“They’re not requesting to go out anymore. They’re just notifying and going and then they’re doing the work,” the source said. “And that circumvents the operational risk management aspect where the technician before who works for the government could say, no, no. You can’t do that right now.”
Elizabeth Doherty, a spokeswoman for the Professional Aviation Safety Specialists union that represents FAA technicians, told CNN the technician’s “orders were to simply let the contractor in the building,” that he “had no direction to help or assist in any way,” and that “no PASS-represented employee was asked to conduct a risk assessment on this particular upgrade.”
CNN asked the FAA about the discrepancy over whether an FAA technician was or was not providing real time oversight of the work.
“There is a lot of information that we’re trying to track down. So things have been changing,” FAA spokeswoman Hannah Walden told CNN by phone. “It could have been a misunderstanding or whatever. So I’m not saying one way or the other right now. I just am saying we’re trying to provide information as we get it.”
In addressing the changes laid out in the 2025 memo, Walden denied oversight has been reduced, saying the policy change “does not change oversight at all. It changes the priority of the work that needs to be done.”
After this story published, Walden sent an additional statement, seeming to contradict what Bedford said publicly on Tuesday about the technician monitoring the upgrade.
“The FAA escort is responsible for providing the L3Harris technician access to and from the building. Because it is L3 equipment, the escort is not there while the technician is doing work,” she said in the statement.
The episode underscores the complications that can arise over a communications system that is operated by the federal government yet is owned by a private company, in this case L3Harris, whose telecom network serves as the communications backbone for the nation’s airspace.
It also comes as Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress to approve another $50 billion to upgrade the nation’s air traffic control system even as lawmakers question how the billions allocated last year were spent.
L3Harris declined to provide any details in response to CNN’s questions.
In a statement to CNN, the company said it is “supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel.”
People sit on the floor as they wait to try and retrieve luggage during delays and cancellations at LaGuardia airport on November 13, 2026 in the Queens borough of New York City. - Adam Gray/Getty Images
A routine job, then chaos
The policy change laid out in the March 2025 memo didn’t come out of nowhere. The sources familiar with what happened before the ground stop said a chronic, yearslong shortage of FAA technicians as well as the Trump administration’s push for speed helped propel it forward.
The result, they believe, was less oversight of the contractor on Friday and a much slower recovery, as the FAA struggled to pinpoint the source of the problem.
L3Harris notified the FAA on November 9 that it planned to carry out maintenance, replacing a router, at a remote FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, with work set to begin at 9 a.m. on Friday, November 13, one of the sources said.
Four days after the notice, the L3Harris worker arrived.
Even the time of day the work was scheduled raised eyebrows, given it was at a time of heavy air traffic. The sources say FAA technicians were not consulted about the best time to carry out this work at this facility.
By that Friday afternoon, the new router was connected and the L3Harris contractor had left the site with no idea of the chaos that was beginning to unfold, the source said.
Hours later, FAA technicians got a call telling them to return to the site to escort the L3Harris engineer back into the facility. The agency scrambled to find the closest available staff to let him in. Hours had passed between the time the engineer had left and the time he returned to retrieve the router, the source said.
A former FAA technician told CNN that, for agency technicians, checking in with air traffic controllers before leaving a site is standard practice. It’s not clear if the L3Harris engineer took this step.
“As a technician, anytime when I was out there … and I did anything, anything at all to the equipment before I left, I would call up the TRACON or the center or the tower, whatever controllers that had the services that I was providing on that equipment. And I would say, ‘I’m getting ready to leave. Everything look good? Everything okay? You got everything?’ They’d be like, ‘yep,’” the former technician said. “It’s just a practice that you do.”
In the immediate aftermath of the ground stop, Duffy was sharply critical of L3Harris, making a point of calling them out in his public remarks.
“We need L3Harris or whoever provided that router to us to do a better job,” Duffy said during his Saturday press conference. “Many of our contractors, many or our partners, they take our money and they provide really poor service to us. Full stop.”
Yet by Tuesday, Bedford sounded a different tone toward L3Harris.
At a news conference, Bedford described the L3Harris contractor who replaced the router as a “highly trained certified engineer, former Air Force veteran, I’m told a generally competent guy doing the work that he has done dozens and dozens of times before.”
Asked what oversight the FAA provides when contractors work at FAA facilities, Bedford also said, “There is a comprehensive risk management process with every installation. And that installation happens whether it’s with a contractor or with an FAA employee.”
Days earlier, Duffy had defended the timing of the work, pointing out that it was at a remote location. He said he didn’t expect the kind of impact seen last Friday at “smaller locations.”
This story has been updated with additional details.
For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

Elizabeth Doherty, a spokeswoman for the Professional Aviation Safety Specialists union that represents FAA technicians, told CNN the technician’s “orders were to simply let the contractor in the building,” that he “had no direction to help or assist in any way,” and that “no PASS-represented employee was asked to conduct a risk assessment on this particular upgrade.”

CNN asked the FAA about the discrepancy over whether an FAA technician was or was not providing real time oversight of the work.

“There is a lot of information that we’re trying to track down. So things have been changing,” FAA spokeswoman Hannah Walden told CNN by phone. “It could have been a misunderstanding or whatever. So I’m not saying one way or the other right now. I just am saying we’re trying to provide information as we get it.”

In addressing the changes laid out in the 2025 memo, Walden denied oversight has been reduced, saying the policy change “does not change oversight at all. It changes the priority of the work that needs to be done.”

After this story published, Walden sent an additional statement, seeming to contradict what Bedford said publicly on Tuesday about the technician monitoring the upgrade.

“The FAA escort is responsible for providing the L3Harris technician access to and from the building. Because it is L3 equipment, the escort is not there while the technician is doing work,” she said in the statement.

The episode underscores the complications that can arise over a communications system that is operated by the federal government yet is owned by a private company, in this case L3Harris, whose telecom network serves as the communications backbone for the nation’s airspace.

It also comes as Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress to approve another $50 billion to upgrade the nation’s air traffic control system even as lawmakers question how the billions allocated last year were spent.

L3Harris declined to provide any details in response to CNN’s questions.

In a statement to CNN, the company said it is “supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel.”

A routine job, then chaos

The policy change laid out in the March 2025 memo didn’t come out of nowhere. The sources familiar with what happened before the ground stop said a chronic, yearslong shortage of FAA technicians as well as the Trump administration’s push for speed helped propel it forward.

The result, they believe, was less oversight of the contractor on Friday and a much slower recovery, as the FAA struggled to pinpoint the source of the problem.

L3Harris notified the FAA on November 9 that it planned to carry out maintenance, replacing a router, at a remote FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, with work set to begin at 9 a.m. on Friday, November 13, one of the sources said.

Four days after the notice, the L3Harris worker arrived.

Even the time of day the work was scheduled raised eyebrows, given it was at a time of heavy air traffic. The sources say FAA technicians were not consulted about the best time to carry out this work at this facility.

By that Friday afternoon, the new router was connected and the L3Harris contractor had left the site with no idea of the chaos that was beginning to unfold, the source said.

Hours later, FAA technicians got a call telling them to return to the site to escort the L3Harris engineer back into the facility. The agency scrambled to find the closest available staff to let him in. Hours had passed between the time the engineer had left and the time he returned to retrieve the router, the source said.

A former FAA technician told CNN that, for agency technicians, checking in with air traffic controllers before leaving a site is standard practice. It’s not clear if the L3Harris engineer took this step.

“As a technician, anytime when I was out there … and I did anything, anything at all to the equipment before I left, I would call up the TRACON or the center or the tower, whatever controllers that had the services that I was providing on that equipment. And I would say, ‘I’m getting ready to leave. Everything look good? Everything okay? You got everything?’ They’d be like, ‘yep,’” the former technician said. “It’s just a practice that you do.”

In the immediate aftermath of the ground stop, Duffy was sharply critical of L3Harris, making a point of calling them out in his public remarks.

“We need L3Harris or whoever provided that router to us to do a better job,” Duffy said during his Saturday press conference. “Many of our contractors, many or our partners, they take our money and they provide really poor service to us. Full stop.”

Yet by Tuesday, Bedford sounded a different tone toward L3Harris.

At a news conference, Bedford described the L3Harris contractor who replaced the router as a “highly trained certified engineer, former Air Force veteran, I’m told a generally competent guy doing the work that he has done dozens and dozens of times before.”

Asked what oversight the FAA provides when contractors work at FAA facilities, Bedford also said, “There is a comprehensive risk management process with every installation. And that installation happens whether it’s with a contractor or with an FAA employee.”

Days earlier, Duffy had defended the timing of the work, pointing out that it was at a remote location. He said he didn’t expect the kind of impact seen last Friday at “smaller locations.”

title: Can Bitcoin Really Reach $100K? A Wall Street Bank's Trimmed Call Meets the Chart
description: Citi cut its Bitcoin target to $99,532 and trimmed Ethereum. With BTC near $63,000 after a steep monthly slide, the chart shows where $75K resistance sits.
fullContent:
Citi has lowered its Bitcoin price target in a fresh research note. The bank also cut its outlook for Ethereum.

The downgrade lands after a sharp monthly slide. Even so, the new target sits far above today's price. Traders now face one question. Can buyers stop the selling before the bank's reduced forecast drifts out of view?

Citi Lowers the Bar to $99,532

Citi, one of the largest US banks, has cut its Bitcoin price target to $99,532. The bank set out the new number in a research note. The figure replaces an earlier, higher target, so the move counts as a downgrade.

Ethereum took a cut too. Citi lowered its target for the second-largest coin to $2,838. Together the two cuts point to a cooler view of the crypto market as a whole.

Several details remain unclear. The note as reported gives no time frame for the target and no conditions attached to it. They also do not spell out the bank's full reasoning for the reduction.

That makes the call only mildly bearish. Citi marked its outlook down, which signals less confidence than before. Yet the new target still sits well above where Bitcoin trades today. Readers can treat it as a lowered ceiling and still see a forecast for higher prices.

A 58% Climb After a 23% Drop

Bitcoin traded near $63,000 on the day, flat over 24 hours. From there, Citi's target requires a gain of about 58%. That is a large climb for any asset.

The recent pace runs the other way. Bitcoin lost about 15% in the past week and roughly 23% over the past month. Selling has sped up lately.

Such a reversal would take two steps. Bitcoin would first have to win back its monthly losses. Then it would need to keep rising well past that point.

What Has to Go Right

First, the selling has to run out of steam. Several conditions need to line up before Citi's target comes into view.

  • Sellers: They need to tire. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 20, deep in oversold territory. Readings this low often come before bounces. They guarantee nothing.
  • Momentum traders: They want the MACD to cross back above its signal line. For now, momentum is still pointing down.
  • Buyers: They must retake the 50-day average near $75K and the 200-day average just above it. Both lines sit overhead and act as a ceiling.
  • Trend followers: Sellers lead the current trend. That leadership has to pass to buyers.

$75K Is the First Proof Point

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

On the daily chart, the first test sits at the red resistance line, the same level where the 50-day average now runs. A daily close back above that zone would be the earliest sign that Citi's call is on track. It would show buyers can absorb the selling that has driven the slide.

One close would not settle it. Buyers would need to hold that level for several sessions and turn the old ceiling into a floor. The 200-day average sits just above, so the two lines form one thick band of overhead supply.

If that band gives way, the next resistance waits near $80K. Clearing it would open a path toward the high $90Ks, where Citi's target lives.

For now, the chart still describes a downtrend. Bitcoin trades below both averages, and each rally so far has met sellers. Until price closes above that first barrier, the path of least resistance points lower.

Where the Call Breaks

The green support line near $59K marks where the call could break. A daily close below it would leave no marked floor underneath. That would push Citi's target much further out of reach.

Over the coming weeks, a close above both averages would support the bullish path. Without it, the call stays in doubt.

title: Lane Kiffin’s roster fight set the stage, Will Wade just threw a grenade in LSU-SEC war with RJ Luis
description: Will Wade sent RJ Luis onto the court against Louisiana-Monroe, escalating LSU's legal war with the SEC after a judge granted the former pro an injunction.
fullContent:
The LSU Tigers officially escalated the legal battle with the SEC on Wednesday night when basketball coach Will Wade sent RJ Luis Jr. off the bench and into the game against Louisiana-Monroe.

Over the past five days, 19th Judicial District Court Judge William Jorden of Baton Rouge granted RJ Luis a preliminary injunction that allowed the LSU Tigers to roster the former professional athlete.

This whole saga stems from the former St. John's player returning to college for another season, after already declaring for the draft following his final game at the collegiate level in March 2025. After signing a 2-way deal at the NBA level, Luis was seeking a return to college, and signed with LSU last spring.

Luis went undrafted in 2025, then ended up signing a 2-way contract with the Utah Jazz.

LSU LATEST BASKETBALL PROGRAM TO TAP INTO G LEAGUE RANKS, SIGNING FORMER PRO GUARD RJ LUIS JR

But, there have always been rules about former professional athletes coming back to college, though that did not stop Will Wade from recruiting RJ Luis to play basketball at LSU after the head coach returned to Baton Rouge.

And, for all of those that thought this was about college football, you were sorely mistaken.

"I'm gonna refer to our university statement from yesterday. I'll be happy to answer any questions on how he played. "Everybody we played tonight is eligible," Will Wade said postgame. 

Over the past three months, LSU had already been fighting the SEC and NCAA over its rules about athletes pursuing an additional year of eligibility based upon the new guidelines that were enacted around players having five years to play five seasons of competition.

This has led to the LSU athletic department having to make a decision on whether to roster two football players one day before the Tigers faced Clemson in Baton Rouge.

Ultimately, the Tigers' administration decided against officially adding the players to the roster.

LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN

That did not stop the legal saga around both LSU and the SEC, after the conference was enjoined in a lawsuit filed by the football players in September that then led to commissioner Greg Sankey taking the stand inside a Baton Rouge courtroom.

Fast-forward two months, and the same situation has been playing out around the basketball court pertaining to RJ Luis.

"They [LSU] are hiding behind a judge, and I don't know why they think they won't ultimately find a way to punish them," one Power-four head basketball coach told OutKick. "They are actually going to fight the conference over one player and watch the world burn in the process?

"I guess they are really not worried about the fallout, because this makes the whole administration look petty. No matter how you feel about the SEC, it's obvious how they [LSU] feel about [Greg] Sankey and their counterparts within the conference."

SEC ACCUSES LSU OF LETTING LANE KIFFIN RUN WILD AS EXPULSION VOTE COMING THURSDAY IN EXPLOSIVE COURT FILING

After the same judge granted Luis an injunction against the SEC that would prohibit them from punishing LSU if it were to roster and play the basketball star this season, a war of legal words has led to a massive kerfuffle within the legal circles.

The SEC stated that it would not impose any type of fines or penalties against LSU after the injunction was granted, but they were clearly testing Will Wade and the Tigers administration on whether they would actually put RJ Luis into a game.

ATTORNEY COMPARES SEC COMMISSIONER GREG SANKEY TO ‘KIM JONG’ IN LSU-RJ LUIS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUIT

On Tuesday, the SEC released a statement that clearly let it be known that they did not agree with how LSU was interpreting a court order. The Tigers did not have to make the decision on actually putting RJ Luis on the court, which is where the main course of this argument starts.

"LSU's decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the Court's order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of [SEC membership]. This is a deeply concerning and disappointing development."

On Wednesday night, the top officially blew off the lid. During their game against UL-Monroe, and mid-way through the first half, Will Wade subbed in RJ Luis.

"He was eligible, and he played," Will Wade said following LSU's win. 

The Tigers head coach did not discuss 

If there ever was an official escalation to a war, this was it.

Not only did LSU defy what the SEC President and Chancellors had voted on in the past three months, they were clearly jumping into the deep end of this very large pool of legal waters that will undoubtably set-off another chain of events that involve legal filings.

The conference wants to be able to enforce its own rules. LSU is using a court's order to waddle around the rules of rostering and playing a former professional athlete by using a Baton Rouge judge as the scapegoat.

INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN

In addition to the arguments made in a Louisiana court, the SEC had filed its own lawsuit against LSU on the same day Commissioner Greg Sankey took the stand in Baton Rouge.

In an Alabama federal court, the SEC sued LSU President Wade Rousse, athletic director Verge Ausberry and other Tiger officials for violating their first amendment rights pertaining to enforcing conference rules.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This has led to both sides exchanging legal jabs, with the latest coming on Wednesday, as the SEC was asking a judge to strike certain language used in a motion-to-dismiss filed by LSU. Legal counsel for the Tigers claimed that the SEC had brought forth "hallucinated" claims against defendants.

A judge ordered LSU lawyers to release a public apology through a press release, which Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill told the court was not going to happen through her own filing.

In addition to the mess going on in an Alabama federal court, RJ Luis' attorney, Tony Clayton, filed a motion to hold the SEC in contempt of court that came in response to the conference's statement on Tuesday night.

"We want to hold [Sankey] and the SEC in contempt for the threat," Tony Clayton said. "Their lawyer sent us an email that they would not take any actions against LSU or threaten any actions. And then Sankey or an SEC official issued the threat about what they're going to do to LSU."

Now, ten minutes into a game against Louisiana-Monroe on Wednesday night, the LSU administration decided to pull the pin and throw the grenade.

title: 'The View' co-host Whoopi Goldberg demands Dems impeach RFK Jr, 'get his a-- out of there'
description: "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded Congress impeach HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. after the U.S. lost its measles elimination status Tuesday.
fullContent:
ABC's "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded that the incoming Democratic Congress impeach U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. after the country lost its measles elimination status Tuesday.

The panel on Wednesday's show discussed the Pan American Health Organization announcing that for the first time in 26 years, the U.S. lost its measles elimination status after more than 5,400 confirmed cases were reported this year.

The hosts largely blamed Kennedy for the outbreak, pointing to his past scrutiny of vaccines as a cause for the rise in cases, with Goldberg going as far as to hold him responsible for measles-related deaths.

RFK JR. BACKTRACKS ON TIMELINE FOR DETERMINING CAUSE OF AUTISM

"I’m just gonna say it: get his a-- out of there!" Goldberg said to a cheering audience. "Just impeach him! Impeach him! Impeach him. I don’t wanna say it, but I feel like he’s responsible for many people not making it. Get him gone, man!"

When co-host Joy Behar remarked that members of President Donald Trump's cabinet could still remain in office for two more years, Goldberg doubled down on Kennedy's impeachment.

"Start with this one!" Goldberg continued. "Start with this one, and then go to [Secretary of War Pete] Hegseth, and then go to the other ones, and get people in these positions who can actually do the damn job! We are tired of this! People are dying! Children are dying! Stop it! Impeach him!"

CHERYL HINES SAYS 'THE VIEW' HOSTS JUST WANTED TO 'GRILL' HER ABOUT RFK JR, DIDN'T TALK ABOUT NEW BOOK

In a comment to Fox News Digital, White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster defended Kennedy and said that the Trump administration has repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, citing an ABC News interview with Trump from April 2025.

"President Trump and Secretary Kennedy have both stated that vaccination is the best way to prevent measles infections. In response to outbreaks, the President and Secretary have repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, coordinated with states, and facilitated the deployment of vaccine doses across the country," Schuster said.

Fox News Digital also reached out to HHS and ABC for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

CNN'S DANA BASH SPARS WITH RFK JR OVER VACCINE EFFICACY, DEMANDS HE 'LOOK INTO THE CAMERA' AND PUSH VACCINES

"The View" panel has frequently criticized Kennedy's leadership, sometimes making extreme accusations. Earlier this year, Behar similarly accused Kennedy of "trying to kill us."

"Here you’ve got a guy who is in charge of our health, who is a former heroin addict ... he swam in sewage! Who does that?" Behar said in April. "And [he] snorted cocaine off a toilet seat. This is who is in charge of your health, America. We’re in a lot of trouble."

title: Kevin O'Leary Tells Gen Z Security Guard Working 80 Hours a Week and Spending 55% of His Pay on Rent 'You're Just Not Looking Hard Enough'
description:
Working more hours is supposed to mean getting ahead. Somewhere between the overtime and the rent check, that deal can fall apart.
“Shark Tank” investor Kevin O’Leary had a simple fix for one young worker stuck in that squeeze. Find a better job, and look harder for it.
“Well, I don’t agree with you,” O’Leary said in a Jubilee “Surrounded" debate posted on YouTube on Sunday. “You’re just not looking hard enough.”
Eighty Hours And Still Short
Security guard Kieran, one of 20 Gen Z workers who took on O’Leary in the debate, laid out his own numbers.
“You say that, and I’m going to use myself as an example, I work 80 hours a week on average,” he said.
“I’m working 80 hours a week, I’m paying 55% of my income just toward rent alone,” he continued.
Kieran said another 40% of his income goes to other bills, and that his job doesn’t leave much room to climb.
“I work a preventative job where I have to wait for something to happen to react to it,” he said, adding that “you can’t really expect the ladder to open up.”
The job hunt hasn’t gone any better. Kieran said he applied to 10 jobs in the past month and got “not a single interview.” Across the past year, he said, hundreds of applications have turned into only a handful of interviews.
“You can’t just say, ‘get a new job,'” Kieran said.
O’Leary Pitches a Promotion
O’Leary steered him toward management, telling him “there’s somebody somewhere that needs a manager of more security guards.”
He said landing that kind of role takes a focused search.
“You’re going to myopically focus on getting one, and you’re going to spend a fair amount of time making sure that happens,” O’Leary said.
“And you’re going to do it over and over again, but I don’t think you’ve written the right resume or you haven’t put a video together that says, ‘Look, I’m really good at this,” he continued. “I understand how to manage people, and I can enhance productivity.'” 
Neither Side Budged
Kieran wasn’t sold.
“I like the idea of getting a better job that has more money involved. But the job market in America just doesn’t allow that currently,” he said.
That’s when O’Leary told him he simply wasn’t looking hard enough.
Kieran’s rent alone puts him past the line the Department of Housing and Urban Development uses for a “severe cost burden,” which the agency defines as monthly housing costs, including utilities, above 50% of monthly income.
A polished resume can open doors, but it can’t lower the rent. O’Leary is betting a sharper pitch and a supervisor title will get Kieran out of the 80-hour grind, while Kieran says he can’t get enough employers to call him back to find out.

title: Dan Ives Stays Bullish on Nvidia Despite Slide: Is the Chip Bigger Than Huang?
description:
Dan Ives stays bullish on Nvidia after its post-Huang slide, even as activists weigh a push to bring the founder back.
The post Dan Ives Stays Bullish on Nvidia Despite Slide: Is the Chip Bigger Than Huang? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Dan Ives stays bullish on Nvidia (NVDA) even without Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive officer (CEO) Nov. 12. The Yorkville Ives & Co. senior managing director now says Huang could still return, as activist investors push for it.

Regardless, Ives still argues the company’s artificial intelligence (AI) chips, not its founder, drive the stock.

Can One Chip Outlast Its Founder?

Huang resigned after details of multiple affairs emerged, and the board said his personal behavior conflicted with the company’s conduct standards.

Still, Ives told Bloomberg that the investment case rests on the chip itself.

“Jensen or no Jensen, it’s one chip in the world fueling AI and it’s Nvidia.”

He sets fair value at $225 a share. He also says Nvidia’s fiscal 2028 revenue growth guidance of 75% could end nearer 85% to 90%.

Shares rose more than 3% in extended trading after Nvidia’s first post-Huang earnings report.

Meanwhile, interim CEO Colette Kress runs the company while executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles looks for a permanent chief.

Who Holds the 15% Needed to Force a Vote?

Nvidia’s bylaws let holders of 15% of voting power who have held it for a year call a special meeting. Nvidia’s proxy credits Huang with 3.58%.

Activist investor Bill Ackman, who founded investment firm Pershing Square Capital, has floated teaming up with Huang. The same proxy lists BlackRock at 7.43% and Vanguard Capital Management at 7.31%.

However, Polymarket, a prediction market, priced Huang rejoining Nvidia near 30% by the end of 2027, per earlier BeInCrypto reporting.

Ives addressed the activist push on Surveillance.

“The activism has surprised me just how loud it is.”

He noted Nvidia has no staggered board and no supermajority voting rule. One meeting could therefore aim to oust the whole board. That would turn a leadership dispute into a test of activist power over a core AI supplier.

title: Binance Plans Expansion into 5 Asian Markets
description: Binance plans to reveal details of its upcoming Asian expansion in early 2027.
fullContent:
Binance is preparing to expand its presence across five Asian markets next year, despite facing one of the biggest security incidents in crypto history.

The exchange has already started discussions with five or six potential markets, and three of those talks are at an advanced stage, according to SB Seker, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head, who spoke to Reuters during the Singapore FinTech Festival.

While he did not reveal which countries are being considered, Seker said South and Southeast Asia remain priorities for the company.

Funding Concerns

Binance expects to share more details about its expansion plans in the first quarter of next year. The report comes shortly after a massive security breach linked to North Korea resulted in $6.3 billion worth of crypto being stolen from the platform last month. Both Binance and the FBI have blamed North Korea for the attack. But Pyongyang has denied any involvement and even went on to call Washington’s accusations a political provocation.

The incident forced Binance to temporarily suspend withdrawals across affected networks, but the exchange has since been restoring access in stages. Seker said Binance had covered 95% of the lost tokens and was aiming to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of this week.

To address the losses, the company used its own funds to buy replacement tokens and worked with other industry players to freeze around $3 billion worth of stolen assets. Binance also confirmed last week that it had completed coverage of the customer assets affected by the breach. Despite the scale of the incident, Seker said the financial impact was manageable and would not force the company to seek additional funding.

He described the amount spent on replacing the stolen tokens as relatively small compared with Binance’s overall financial position, adding that the exchange could absorb the cost without changing how it operates.

Regulatory Response

Seker also revealed Binance contacted regulators in markets including Japan, South Korea, Australia, Thailand and New Zealand within 36 to 48 hours of the breach to address the extent and the circumstances surrounding the attack.

The crypto exchange does not have a formally established headquarters, but it has identified the Abu Dhabi Global Market’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) as its primary regulator and pays taxes wherever required by local laws.

title: Fred Warner calls Mexico City NFL game 'super special' as Mexican roots take center stage
description: Fred Warner, who leads the 49ers with 88 tackles, calls returning to Mexico City "super special" as San Francisco preps at high elevation for the Vikings.
fullContent:
This week’s NFL international schedule will feature a return trip to Mexico City.

The San Francisco 49ers last played in Mexico City in 2022, and this Sunday they will be back in Mexico's capital city for a Week 11 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings. The trip also has personal significance for linebacker Fred Warner, whose maternal grandfather was born in Mexico.

Warner’s grandfather died when Warner’s mother, Laura, was young, and Warner never had the opportunity to meet him. He has nevertheless spoken about his connection to Mexican culture, including the Spanish language he heard and spoke at home as a child.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Warner acknowledged the significance of Sunday night's game.

"Super special," he said after practice on Wednesday. "I remember that first time around, didn’t know what exactly what to expect, but I think that was my first time being out of the country and playing in a game of that magnitude."

Warner, the NFL's current leading tackler, took in a World Cup match at Estadio Azteca over the summer and recalled the electric environment.

"That was elite," Warner said. "Soccer, or football as they call it, the World Cup, representing your home country, that is a whole different animal. The NFL obviously is elite as well, but that was that was a once-in-a-lifetime experience."

NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT'

San Francisco beat Arizona 38-10 in Mexico City on Nov. 21, 2022, and the team is following the same blueprint to prepare for Sunday night's game. After defeating the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, the Niners flew to Colorado so they could practice at the Air Force Academy, where the 7,258-foot elevation is nearly equal to Mexico City, hoping to gain an advantage for the NFL’s final international game of 2026.

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan recalled some of the stressful elements that came along with the 2022 Mexico City trip, including the bus carrying players getting lost on the way to the stadium.

"Usually our last bus of players gets three hours before the game, and they got lost somehow on the way to the stadium," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "They didn’t get there until an hour and 15 minutes before the game, and had like 12 starters on it. So that was somewhat stressful, but it didn’t affect us."

The 49ers enter Sunday at 8-1 and atop the NFC standings. The Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins at last week's trade deadline, returning the veteran quarterback to the franchise where he spent six seasons.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: President Trump downplays panic over tech outages: ‘Nobody’s going to play games with us’
description: President Donald Trump urged Americans to "relax" over FAA and Microsoft outages, warning any country that targeted U.S. systems would be hit hard.
fullContent:
President Donald Trump sought to reassure Americans concerned about a series of technology disruptions over the past week, urging them to "relax" and saying no country would dare "play games" with U.S. digital infrastructure.

Trump’s remarks in China follow a slew of outages affecting the Federal Aviation Administration, Microsoft, major U.S. banks and other institutions, disrupting air travel and business operations and putting Americans on edge.

"Tell them to relax. Everything's good," the president told Fox News senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich.

TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

"I don't want to use specific names because they're treating me extremely well in China, and I have a lot of respect and a lot of relationships and a good relationship with President Xi. But if anybody did that to us, and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me," the commander in chief said on "The Ingraham Angle." 

"Nobody's going to play games with us."

Trump, who said the outages were unrelated, warned that any bad actors should know better than to target U.S. technological infrastructure.

"They know they would be hit so hard," the president said. 

RECENT SERVICE OUTAGES NOT STATE-SPONSORED ATTACKS, DNI JAY CLAYTON TESTIFIES

"These are individual events. ... I'll let you know if there's a problem."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed Congress in part for the hours-long nationwide ground stop, arguing the system is outdated because the government has not provided the agency with sufficient funding to modernize its technology.

"They're putting in new equipment, and things happen when you put in new equipment," Trump said.

FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP

"This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed. And it's gone down before, and we did the right thing. Nobody was injured. Nobody was hurt. No planes were bunking into each other," he continued.

Trump told Fox News that Duffy is doing "fantastic," standing behind the transportation chief over his handling of Friday’s nationwide ground stop.

He echoed Duffy’s concerns about the state of the system, saying that while the United States has money available, he believes it is better to wait for additional funding and pursue a complete overhaul rather than "piecemeal," patchwork renovations.

"We were given $12 million, but I said, 'Don't spend it until we can do the whole thing, the whole system. You don't want to do piecemeal,'" Trump said.

"We want to give out ... like the big, beautiful deal, one big, beautiful contract," he proposed. "We want to give out a contract to somebody that can coordinate everything."

The president touted his building background and said that with his plan, the United States will have the best air traffic control system in the world.

"I build very well. I've made a lot of money building things, always, and I know how to do this stuff," he said.

title: Ella Langley dominates CMA Awards with major wins as Taylor Swift makes stunning return to stage
description: Ella Langley dominates the CMAs as she wins big while Taylor Swift makes her return after decade-long absence.
fullContent:
The 60th annual Country Music Association Awards took place live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday night.

Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night. 

While accepting the award, she joked that the crowd must be sick of her already, getting a laugh from those in the room.

"This isn't real life," she said while accepting the award. "Thank you Jesus, I'm at a loss for words," she added, before saying, "This has been the most special night.

As she swept all the categories she was nominated in, Lainey Wilson brought out a bedazzled broom for her, telling her she knew she had it prepared as she knew Langley was going to sweep the show. 

Langley also won music video of the year before the broadcast. "Choosin' Texas" was named as the music video of the year winner during Good Morning America Wednesday morning. The record-breaking hit, also won single of the year and song of the year. 

Later in the show, Langley got teary-eyed as she accepted the award for album of the year, for her album, "Dandelion," noting it took two years to make. She was speechless while accepting the award and received a standing ovation from the audience.

"I’m at a loss for words. I don’t know what to say," she said in her speech. "I love country music and I love what I do."

Her wins also resulted in two wins for Miranda Lambert, who is credited as a producer on the song. 

Langley continued her winning streak later on in the show when she took home the award for female vocalist of the year, beating out Lambert, Musgraves, Moroney and Wilson for the honor.

"I have so much love and respect for every single person and every single woman in this category," she said while accepting the award. "This is what I have lived and breathed not only just the past seven years that I moved to Nashville, but genuinely my whole entire life. I haven’t wanted to do another thing. There wasn’t anything on my heart. I never had a plan B. I was never gonna have a plan b. If I was still playing cover gigs with a tip jar out in front of me for four hours I’d still be doing this."

Rising star Langley led the pack with 9 nominations, tying Lainey Wilson and Lambert's all-time record for the most nods by a female artist in a single year. Her win for single of the year left Taylor Swift going home empty-handed tonight, which didn't stop Taylor Swift from cheering for her as she went up to accept the award.

Swift made her big return to the CMA Awards – after last attending in 2016. Her single, "I Knew It, I Knew You," is nominated for single of the year.

The singer took the stage to perform at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years, starting her performance with her nominated song, before transitioning into one of her classic hits, "Our Song." 

Lambert also had a moment on stage with Kacey Musgraves, when the two sang their hit duet, "Horses and Divorces," from Musgraves' latest album, "Middle of Nowhere."

The song references the rumored feud between the two singers, with them patching things up earlier this year.

Zach Top honored veteran and military families, bringing one on stage and surprising them with the return of their son from service.

In addition to her performance with Musgraves, Lambert took the stage once again with Langley to sing their song, "Snakeskin Boots" for the first time on television. The two matched in their versions of brown dresses with snakeskin print and fringe as they commanded the stage during their performance.

Brooks and Dunn won vocal duo of the year for the 17th time in a row at this year’s award show. In addition, the duo also received the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award, which was presented to them by Swift.

Prior to Swift handing them the award, Luke Bryan took to the stage alongside Brothers Osborne, HARDY, Marcus King, and Halestorm to pay tribute to the iconic duo.

Little Big Town announced Chris Stapleton as the winner of male vocalist of the year. The musician took the stage earlier in the evening with both Mumford & Sons to sing "Here" and Stephen Wilson Jr. to sing, "I’m a Song."

During his speech he encouraged fans to follow their dreams, and dedicated the award to his mother, who died last year around this time.

"She always told me that I could be whatever I wanted to be, and turns out that was true," he said. 

Lady A introduced Tim McGraw to the stage to perform, "Don’t Take the Girl" for the first time on the CMA stage, as he is one of the Country Music Hall of Fame inductees this year. It was an intimate performance with the majority of the stage lights turned off save for a few spotlights behind him.

Wilson returned to host the event for the third consecutive time, her second solo. Wilson is also nominated for entertainer of the year, which she won in 2023 and 2025.

She also took to the stage during the show to perform her hit song, "Just A Woman."

Megan Moroney blew fans away while strumming on her pink guitar as she sang "Beautiful Things" into her pink microphone. During her performance, fans surrounding the stage held up pink roses, while everyone in the arena swayed to the beat as with their flashlights lighting up the crowd.

Tucker Wetmore got the crowd pumped with his performance of "Who Told You That," encouraging the crowd to get up and dance. While singing he enthusiastically played the piano which was surrounded by a circle of fire on the stage.

The show began with a tribute to Dolly Parton. Parton was one of the most decorated figures in CMA Awards history, earning 45 nominations and winning 10 trophies over her career, including entertainer of the year in 1978, two female vocalist of the year awards, and the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.

Beyond her wins, she also helped define the telecast itself, famously co-hosting the ceremony in 1988 and returning in 2019 to co-host alongside Carrie Underwood and Reba McEntire.

'GOD HAS BEEN SO GOOD TO ME': ELLA LANGLEY REACTS TO INCREDIBLE NINE CMA AWARDS NOMINATIONS

Parton died on August 25, 2026, at age 80 in Nashville following a brief, private battle with cancer, roughly a year and a half after the passing of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

At the start of the show, Wilson made lighthearted jokes about Swift and Travis Kelce's mega Madison Square Garden wedding.

WATCH: Michael Ray returns to CMA Awards after taking a break to record new music

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

While Swift, Wilson and Langley have already taken the stage for solo performances,  Luke Combs, Megan Moroney,  The Red Clay Strays, Tucker Wetmore, Vince Gill, and Zach Top are still set to perform.

Cody Johnson was initially slated to perform at the 2026 CMA Awards, but the four-time nominee and entertainer of the year contender pulled out of attending and performing at tonight’s ceremony, announcing a day prior that he had to step away due to mental and physical exhaustion.

title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell's mother sues Marriott over twin's death, hotel counters with 911 audio
description: April Moore says a hotel worker knocked during CPR and no AED was available as she sues Marriott International over daughter Kierston Russell's death.
fullContent:
April Moore, mother of Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell, is suing AC Hotel Tuscaloosa Downtown and Marriott International over the death of her daughter, Kierston Russell.

Details of the wrongful death suit surfaced ahead of a Dec. 7 hearing in Tuscaloosa County Circuit Court.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Russell has thrown for nearly 2,500 yards and 21 touchdowns this season. Off the field, his family is pursuing a jury trial over the events of June 3, 2025. Kierston, his 18-year-old twin sister, planned to enroll at Alabama alongside him.

Per defense filings, Moore and Keelon left their room around 7:20 p.m. after Kierston reported stomach pain and irregular sleep.

Moore returned, found Kierston unresponsive on the bathroom floor, called 911 at 9:55 p.m., and started CPR. Kierston died at DCH Regional Medical Center.

TWO MEN DIE AFTER SUSPECTED ELECTROCUTION AT HOTEL POOL AS RESCUE EFFORT INJURES OTHERS

Moore sued on June 15, 2026, accusing the hotel and Marriott of failing to train staff in CPR or provide a defibrillator. Her complaint states a worker knocked on the door during the emergency, forcing Moore to stop compressions to answer it, and offered no aid.

Plaintiff's attorney Derrick Mills said experts believe an AED would have saved Kierston's life, adding the hotel "literally frustrated April's efforts in trying to revive her daughter."

The defense disputes that account using timestamps.

In court filings, the defendants say 911 dispatchers never called the front desk, and staff responded only after a guest reported screaming. They contend 911 audio shows Moore never stopped CPR to open the door, requiring a worker to unlock it with a master key before EMTs began treatment within three minutes.

The defense also says 911 calls and bodycam photos place an AED in the room within three to five minutes, adding Alabama law did not require one. Defense counsel Rebecca Young declined comment.

FORMER CLEVELAND BROWNS WR DAVID BELL SEEKS $300M AFTER BOTCHED SURGERY ALLEGEDLY NEARLY KILLED HIM

To reach a jury under Alabama law, Moore must clear two hurdles: proving the hotel owed a duty beyond summoning paramedics, and proving its response cost Kierston her life.

Marriott and the hotel requested dismissal in October; Moore moved to seal records and filed a non-public response on Nov. 6, setting up a Dec. 7 showdown in court.

title: Bukele gets hero’s welcome from afar as thousands rally in Haiti after gang crackdown
description: Thousands marched in Haiti to thank Nayib Bukele for sending troops to battle violent gangs, prompting an emotional response from the Salvadoran president.
fullContent:
Thousands of people in Haiti took to the streets Tuesday in a show of support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deploying troops to the country to combat violent armed gangs.

The demonstration unfolded as Haiti's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Patrick Pélissier, prepared to travel to San Salvador to discuss anti-gang strategies and ongoing troop cooperation.

The president reflected on the moment in a post on X, sharing a video capturing a sea of people chanting, dancing and cheering in celebration.

"I never expected anything like this. I hear you loud and clear. I love you too. We will triumph. God will give us victory," Bukele said.

BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR

According to Reuters, some demonstrators carried signs reading "Long live Bukele" and "Down with the gangs," while others voiced their support for the Salvadoran leader.

"Only a week of operation, we can see the path to change in Haiti. We say thank you to Bukele for all the help he gives us," demonstrator Claudy Mayas said.

Another demonstrator said Bukele was providing Haitians with the one thing they had been waiting years for.

"Four years ago, I could not go to Champs de Mars. I couldn't go to the south of Haiti," a demonstrator, also identified as Claude, said.

"We don’t ask much of the government. We don’t ask for jobs. We need only security."

ROBOT DOGS MOUNTED WITH RIFLES DEPLOYED IN ANTI-GANG STADIUM OPERATION IN HAITI

Just two weeks ago, Bukele backed an operation involving devastating airstrikes that destroyed the headquarters of 400 Mawozo, one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs. The home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, was also targeted in the operation, Bukele previously said.

The direct military action marked a dramatic escalation in Haiti's fight against years of severe gang violence and insecurity.

Bukele joined the mission after four Salvadoran members of the U.N.-backed anti-gang force went missing in a suspected gang ambush near Port-au-Prince on Oct. 18. At the time, Bukele sent more than 2,000 troops to Haiti.

EL SALVADOR-BACKED AIR ASSAULT DESTROYS HAITI GANG HEADQUARTERS AMID SEARCH FOR MISSING TROOPS

While residents paraded through the streets in celebration, U.N. officials issued a statement Tuesday reminding leaders that anti-gang operations must prioritize civilian protection.

"Security forces must strictly limit the use of lethal force to situations where it is unavoidable to protect life from an imminent threat and as a last resort," the agency said.

According to the U.N., armed gangs control an estimated 80% to 90% of Haiti's capital and are expanding into surrounding regions.

Between January and October 2026 alone, the U.N. documented nearly 4,600 people killed, alongside the wider displacement of nearly 1.5 million people.

title: Mayor of US city with largest Muslim population calls El-Sayed's election 'an American story'
description: Sen. Abdul El-Sayed's historic win drew praise from Dearborn's mayor, who calls the first Muslim American elected to the Senate a truly American story.
fullContent:
The mayor of the first Arab-majority city in the U.S., home to one of the largest Muslim populations per capita in the nation, told Fox News Digital Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s election to the U.S. Senate was "monumental."

"It was monumental, and it's [truly] an American story where the brightest and best of us was elevated to one of the highest offices in the world — a member of the United States Senate — and where the people of Michigan elected an individual regardless of the direction in which he prays, but rather based on the direction in which he wishes to lead," Dearborn, Michigan, Mayor Abdullah Hammoud told Fox News Digital.

"I think that is truly a beautifully American story."

NYC'S MAMDANI SAYS ABDUL EL-SAYED'S SENATE VICTORY IN MICHIGAN 'MEANS SO MUCH TO SO MANY'

Hammoud's comments followed El-Sayed’s Nov. 3 victory over former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in Michigan's high-stakes race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. With the win, El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat and former Detroit health director, became the first Muslim American elected to the U.S. Senate.

In his victory speech in Detroit shortly after the race was called, El-Sayed took direct aim at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). The pro-Israel lobbying group and its affiliates poured roughly $30 million into the August Democratic primary to back U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens against El-Sayed, and he thanked the group for the chance to "beat you twice." 

Celebrating his victory, El-Sayed also invoked the Arabic phrase "Alhamdulillah," which translates to "Praise be to God."

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

Throughout the campaign, El-Sayed faced repeated scrutiny over his rhetoric on Israel, concerns among some Jewish voters in Michigan and allegations of family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, claims El-Sayed rejected. He also drew criticism from fellow Democrats over his campaign appearances alongside controversial far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who previously faced backlash over incendiary remarks regarding the Sept. 11 attacks and Israel.

Three days after his win, El-Sayed addressed the Arab America Foundation’s Connect Empowerment Summit in Chantilly, Virginia, just outside Washington, D.C., where he referred to Michigan as the "capital of Arab America."

"I know we’re here in D.C., which, of course, is the capital of the United States of America. But Michigan is the capital of Arab America," El-Sayed said.

During the speech, El-Sayed also pushed back against the attacks he faced on the campaign trail, saying opponents "wanted to make this a referendum on me and my name and my faith."

ASRA NOMANI: EL-SAYED GLIDES INTO ROLE AS ROCK STAR OF THE HARD LEFT'S RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Hammoud, who became Dearborn’s first Arab American and Muslim mayor in 2022, explained to Fox News Digital what El-Sayed meant by calling Michigan the "capital of Arab America."

"I think he's just speaking to the idea that the largest concentration of Arab Americans happens to be in the city of Dearborn, just [as] you have so many other cities across America celebrating the unique demographic — sometimes the largest of X population residing within their city bounds — no different," Hammoud said.

fullContent:
Strategy’s Stretch (STRC) fell as low as $96.01 on Wednesday. That is about 4% below the $100 level the company has defended for weeks.

Bitcoin slid the same day. It briefly broke below $63,000, touching $62,069, before recovering. Strategy holds 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452, so Bitcoin’s low sat about 17% below that.

Is the 12% Dividend Still Being Paid?

Strategy kept STRC’s rate at 12% for December, according to its Nov. 16 filing. Management plans to hold that rate until STRC trades steadily near $100.

STRC is preferred stock, which pays income ahead of common shareholders and never matures. Strategy resets the rate monthly to keep the price near $100.

The payout is not guaranteed. Strategy’s own STRC page warns the dividend could fall significantly.

Who Is Paying to Hold STRC at $100?

Strategy bought back $228.1 million of STRC last week and $188.3 million the week before. Most of that cash came from selling new shares of its common stock (MSTR).

New shares shrink each existing owner’s slice. MSTR traded near $93 on Wednesday, below STRC itself, per TradingView.

“STRC getting hammered today, worse than BTC despite buyback support,” noted Matthew Sigel, head of digital assets research at VanEck.

Earlier that day, Strategy posted a chart saying Bitcoin beat its 2.6% yearly “breakeven” return in every four-year window since 2015.

Strategy’s post used prices up to the November 17 close, a day before STRC fell to $96.01 and Bitcoin briefly dipped towards $62,000.

It measures four-year holds, but STRC buyers who paid near $100 were down over 4% on Wednesday, and MSTR has lost about 36% since November 4.

Strategy still has room to act. It has $332.2 million left for preferred buybacks and $18.1 billion of MSTR it can sell, after it halved its Bitcoin buying last week.

BeInCrypto noted on November 4 that STRC’s last $100 run, in May, lasted four sessions before Bitcoin dragged it lower. This one held into mid-November.

Monday’s filing will show whether Strategy keeps buying STRC back, and how many new MSTR shares that costs.

The post Is MicroStrategy’s 12% Dividend Safe? Its $100 Stock Just Broke Again appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Mamdani grilled on rhetoric toward Oct 7, combating antisemitism as Jewish New Yorkers fear current climate
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended his Oct. 7 X post at The New York Times' DealBook Summit, telling Andrew Ross Sorkin there must be room to mourn everyone.
fullContent:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was grilled Wednesday on his efforts to combat antisemitism during his appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit.

After greeting his "comrades" at the beginning of his sit-down, Mamdani was pressed by The New York Times' Andrew Ross Sorkin about the importance of "language," specifically in relation to the Jewish community in New York City and growing antisemitism.

Sorkin pointed to Mamdani's controversial X post commemorating the Oct. 7 terrorist attack committed against Israel, which dedicated more words toward the plight of the Palestinians and Israel's military response in Gaza than the roughly 1,200 Israelis who were brutally murdered that day by Hamas.

BILL MAHER MOCKS MAMDANI FOR PIVOTING TO ISRAEL CRITICISM IN OCT 7 TRIBUTE, CALLS IT 'TONE-DEAF'

"The head of the Reform Jewish movement (had) said at the time that they thought that the statement made New Yorkers less safe. And then there was a rabbi who said — they called himself a fan of yours — he said, 'Can we just have one day?'" Sorkin told Mamdani. 

"And I'm curious, again, about the language you use. And the reason I mention it is, you know, 53%, I think, of hate crimes in New York City are against Jews.

"And, so, when you use language in this regard — and I know we can have a whole debate about whether condemning Israel gets conflated with antisemitism and this and that — but do you feel like there's an extra sort of responsibility or distinction in the language you use when you use it?"

Mamdani pushed back at the premise of the question, saying his X post "doesn't cover the entirety of the day," which included a vigil honoring the Oct. 7 victims, noting that he was also protested for attending the vigil.

"My politics is one that believes that there has to be room to mourn everyone," Mamdani said. 

"And what I sought to do not only in the statement, but also in my physical attendance at that vigil, which I had attended the year before, was to make clear that I will oppose with every bone in my body the violations of international law, no matter who commits them, who conducts them. And that's why I've called Oct. 7 a war crime. And that is why I have also been immensely critical of the Israeli government as well."

MAMDANI DINED AT NYC RESTAURANT LINKED TO ANTI-ISRAEL MENU AFTER BEING BOOED AT OCT 7 VIGIL: REPORT

The democratic socialist mayor slammed the "objectionable" statistic that Jewish New Yorkers are the victims of more than half of all hate crimes despite being 10-12% of the city's population.

"That, to me, is unacceptable, because in addition to being proud of being the mayor of New York City, I'm also proud to be the mayor of the most Jewish city in the United States of America," Mamdani told Sorkin. 

"So much of what so many of us love about New York is tied up in that same legacy. And to me, the responsibility is you have to root out antisemitism. You have to root out any form of bigotry.

"And that there will be, and there are, Jewish New Yorkers, as well as New Yorkers of other faiths or no faiths at all, who disagree with me on my views on Israel and Palestine," the mayor continued. "There's no question. My job is to still deliver for them as well, and to deliver them the best possible city, because, at the end of the day, they live in the same city."

"I get it," Sorkin interjected. "My question is, would you ever think about sending out one tweet on Oct. 7, saying how terrible what happened on Oct. 7 was, and then waiting till Oct. 8 to say how terrible you think Israel has handled the situation?"

Sorkin's follow-up question sparked applause from the audience.

MAMDANI’S ANTISEMITISM PLAN DRAWS CRITICISM AS RABBIS SAY IT AVOIDS KEY DRIVER OF HATE

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

"When the Israeli government is conducting a genocide of Palestinians, oftentimes the defense that will be given, no matter what day that it's asked about, will be the relationship to Oct. 7," Mamdani responded. 

"My point being, this is a day that is not only a horrific war crime. It is also a day that has been used as a justification for all that followed it. And it is in that day that it is important, like in any day, to mourn the totality of its impact."

Mamdani insisted he understands "the other side" of the argument but doubled down on his stance.

"I have a politics of universality. Whenever I'm asked about 'Why do you support Palestinian freedom or Palestinian rights?' I speak about the importance of extending these same values, of empathy. And that is who I am," he added.
