title: Musk says he feels 'foolish' after spending over $440 million to back Republicans
description:
Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, expressed buyer’s remorse Wednesday about his massive — and ultimately futile — spending spree to elect Republicans in the midterms.
The SpaceX and Tesla founder, who spent over $440 million backing GOP candidates, most of whom lost, acknowledged: “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.” The comments came during The New York Times’ DealBook Summit, where Musk also distanced himself from President Donald Trump’s MAGA movement, maintaining “there are positives and negatives in both parties.”
“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much. Or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said at the event, which he attended virtually from China, as he and other business leaders accompanied President Donald Trump to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. “But it certainly shows that American elections are not just about money.”
Musk, who has experienced an on-again off-again relationship with Trump, was by far the biggest single donor this election cycle, spending at an unprecedented clip to support Republicans. But his efforts failed to make a major impact, as key GOP strongholds such as Texas, where he spent the bulk of his money, and Kansas flipped to Democrats.
Despite his midterm spending, Musk sought to clarify during Wednesday’s public interview that he is “not MAGA” — regardless of his ties with the president. Instead, Musk claimed he supported a balance of power between Democrats and Republicans in the government.
“I’m not sure what MAGA means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that,” Musk said.
These statements conflict with how Musk aligned with Trump in the past, even going as far to label himself as “Dark MAGA” when he campaigned for him just two years ago.
In fact, Musk appeared optimistic about working with the newly elected Democratic governor in Texas, where he runs massive SpaceX and Tesla operations. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, who has criticized the tech billionaire, has also said she is open to a “strong working relationship” with Musk.
“The new governor, actually, I think, is going to be quite moderate,” Musk said. “I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor. And based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor.”
This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/18/musk-says-he-feels-foolish-after-gop-election-spending-spree-01174509

title: Bitcoin Dominance Is Falling, But the Money Isn't Going to Altcoins
description:
Bitcoin dominance lost 60% as USDT dominance jumped 24%. See why the drop does not signal altcoin season yet.
The post Bitcoin Dominance Is Falling, But the Money Isn't Going to Altcoins appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Bitcoin dominance has slipped 2.9% from its Nov. 12 high and dropped below the 60% level. The decline would normally raise hopes of a rotation into altcoins.

The data points elsewhere. USDT dominance has climbed 23.87% from support this month, which suggests traders are parking funds in stablecoins. That mix points to a defensive market, not the start of altcoin season.

Analyst Warns Against Reading the Bitcoin Dominance Drop as Altseason

Bitcoin (BTC) dominance measures Bitcoin’s share of the total crypto market capitalization. On the two-week chart, it fell 1.97% in the current candle to 59.57% on Wednesday.

The candle opened at 60.77% and still has four days left before it closes. Since mid-2025, the metric has traded in a range between roughly 58% and 61%.

The chart also maps a projected path toward 38%, labeled “Altcoin Season 3.0.” According to its annotations, previous drops into the 36% to 40% area coincided with the altcoin rallies of 2017–2018 and 2021.

However, crypto analyst Don Wedge cautioned against that reading.

In his view, a genuine altseason signal appears only when Bitcoin dominance and USDT dominance decline together.

Bitcoin Dominance Slips Below 60% After a Failed Breakout

The daily chart adds detail to the move. Since June, Bitcoin dominance has climbed inside an ascending parallel channel.

On November 12, the metric pushed above the channel’s upper boundary and the 60.5% to 61% resistance zone. It peaked at 61.10%, extending the breakout attempt flagged last week.

The breakout failed almost immediately. Dominance then dropped 2.91% to 59.32% at press time. It also lost 60%, a level that has acted as a pivot since August.

The metric is now testing the lower boundary of the channel. A daily close below it would confirm the breakdown.

Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has fallen to around 30, its lowest reading since early June. That oversold level preceded a rebound in June, so a short-term relief bounce remains possible.

If the decline continues, the next supports sit at 58.54% and in the 58% zone. Notably, the 58% area also marks the floor of the 16-month range on the two-week chart.

USDT Dominance Surges 23.87% Toward Key Resistance

Tether (USDT) dominance tracks USDT’s share of the total crypto market capitalization. It rises when traders sell crypto for stablecoins or when the overall market value shrinks.

In late September, USDT dominance slipped below 6.6% and bottomed near 6.25%. However, it reclaimed the level in mid-October, turning the breakdown into a fakeout.

The 6.6% support held again in late October and early November. From there, USDT dominance rallied 23.87% to the 8.25% resistance.

That level acted as support between June and August. A wick toward 8.4% failed to hold, and the metric now trades at 8.249%, up 2.96% on the day.

The RSI stands near 75, deep in overbought territory and at its highest since early June. A daily close above 8.25% could open the way to 8.6%–8.7%, then the June highs near 9.3%.

Why Falling Bitcoin Dominance Does Not Mean Altcoin Season

Taken together, the charts show Bitcoin losing market share to stablecoins rather than to altcoins.

Supply data adds context. Stablecoin supply fell $14.2 billion in the 30 days through November 9, according to Glassnode. That marked the sharpest contraction since June 2022.

With supply shrinking, rising USDT dominance likely reflects falling crypto valuations rather than fresh Tether issuance. Some capital is parking in USDT, while some is leaving crypto entirely through redemptions.

Altcoin data points the same way. The Altcoin Season Index stood at 39 on November 4, far below the 75 threshold for altseason.

Still, cash held in stablecoins stays within reach of the market. It could flow back quickly if sentiment improves.

What Bitcoin Dominance at 58% and USDT Dominance at 8.25% Could Signal Next

Two levels may decide the next phase for altcoins. These are 58% on Bitcoin dominance and 8.25% on USDT dominance.

For now, Bitcoin dominance falling while USDT dominance rises fits the broad risk-off scenario. A rejection at 8.25% on USDT dominance would offer the first sign of real rotation into altcoins.

The post Bitcoin Dominance Is Falling, But the Money Isn't Going to Altcoins appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Nvidia Moves Up Raises and Stock Grants After Jensen Huang Exit
description:
Nvidia moves staff raises and stock grants to December after Jensen Huang's exit as employees press the board on its CEO search.
The post Nvidia Moves Up Raises and Stock Grants After Jensen Huang Exit appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Nvidia will pay employees raises and grant extra stock in December, months ahead of schedule, interim CEO Colette Kress told staff on Nov. 18. The early payout comes as the chipmaker faces questions over how it will keep talent through a leadership change. Pay topped the list of more than 700 questions staff submitted before the meeting, WIRED reported.

The pledge answers one demand but not the other. Staff’s second most common request was more transparency from the board on who will run Nvidia next. Kress made no matching commitment. Investors raised a related worry a day earlier. A Bank of America analyst asked Kress how Nvidia would retain talent.

Why Nvidia Is Paying Staff Early

Kress, Nvidia’s former finance chief, became interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12. The all-hands was her first address to the nearly 49,000-person workforce. She delivered the pay news within minutes.

“So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” read an excerpt in the report, citing Kress.

On the Nov. 17 earnings call, Kress said stabilizing staff was “probably the most important thing” leadership was weighing.

Will the Board Bring Jensen Huang Back?

Nvidia’s board is weighing internal and external candidates for permanent CEO but has set no timeline.

Thousands of employees had apparently lobbied for Huang’s return, with the former CEO saying he would return if asked. However, board chair Harvey Jones ruled that out the same day.

Co-founder Chris Malachowsky told the meeting that Nvidia’s culture lives in how employees work, not on posters.

“We’re going to be fine,” he said.

The raises arrive in December, but the board has set no date to name Huang’s successor.

fullContent:
Gold hit a 14-month towards $3,700 an ounce on Wednesday. Economist Peter Schiff says traders are wrong to expect more Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Gold holders have taken the loss as traders price in a December Fed hike. Yet Schiff argues a hard tightening cycle would crash stock, bond, and housing markets.

What Pushed Gold to a 14-Month Low?

Gold slid to its 14-month low on Wednesday as a stronger US dollar weighed on the metal. Fed officials added pressure by arguing for further hikes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said persistent inflation could justify a half-point rate hike in December.

Meanwhile, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy may need several more increases.

New York Fed President John Williams, however, said the central bank still has work to do on inflation.

CME Group’s FedWatch Tool, built on fed funds futures, shows a 95% chance of a quarter-point December hike. A half-point move carries nearly 5%.

Would a Volcker-Style Fed Break the Markets?

Peter Schiff is chief economist at Euro Pacific Asset Management and a longtime gold advocate. He says gold traders are pricing in the Fed’s biggest inflation fight since Paul Volcker’s tenure as chair.

“If so, the stock, bond, and real estate markets will crash, and the resulting financial crisis will make 2008 look like a Sunday school picnic.”

Peter Schiff, writing on X

Schiff reasons that a campaign on that scale would crash markets, so he rejects the premise.

Still, Fed officials point to a different risk. Waller has said a quarter-point move alone would put the Fed’s credibility at risk if inflation stays broad.

The Dec. 8-9 meeting will test whether that tightening bias holds as stock, bond, and housing markets absorb higher rates.

title: Police costs for 2028 Olympics could hit $4 billion, LAPD chief says
description:
Los Angeles Police Department Chief Jim McDonnell talks to reporters at LAPD headquarters in March. (Jason Armond / Los Angeles Times)
The estimated cost to protect more than 11,000 athletes, officials, dignitaries and a crush of fans at the 2028 Summer Olympics has jumped to between $3.5 billion and $4 billion, Los Angeles Police Chief Jim McDonnell said in an interview Wednesday.
The new estimate from the chief is markedly higher than anything public officials have announced before — and far above the $1 billion that the U.S. Congress approved last year for policing the massive sporting event.
Los Angeles leaders expect money from last year’s federal action to be distributed sometime in 2027, with dozens of police agencies expected to submit formal proposals soon for a share of the $1 billion.
“The billion dollars is certainly helpful, but that’s not going to cover the cost of just policing Los Angeles for the Olympic Games, during that period of time,” McDonnell said in his interview with The Times. 
 “I think that is about $1.3 billion that we’re going to need” in Los Angeles alone, McDonnell said. “And then to police all of the other venues, I think it’s probably going to be closer to [a total of] $3.5 to $4 billion.”
The Olympic organizers don’t have money set aside for security outside of event venues. And no one has yet determined who will pay if security costs balloon above $1 billion.
The police chief’s comments came ahead of a meeting at the U.S. Secret Service’s offices in downtown Los Angeles on Wednesday, where he and other law enforcement leaders convened for a quarterly meeting on security for the Olympics and Paralympics. The Secret Service is coordinating the effort because the Department of Homeland Security has declared the sports extravaganzas National Special Security Events.
An LAPD spokesman said the chief got those figures after conversations with many of the dozens of law enforcement leaders who are coordinating safety plans.
Los Angeles County Sheriff Robert Luna and California Highway Patrol Commissioner Sean Duryee told The Times they had also had been informed that the total security estimate had climbed to $3 billion or more.
It remains unclear if McDonnell will be overseeing much of the Olympic security surge, as L.A. Mayor-elect Nithya Raman previously suggested she would replace him as chief, perhaps before the Summer Games, which open on July 14, 2028.
In the interview, McDonnell expressed optimism about working cooperatively with the mayor-elect, citing a two-hour phone conversation he had with Raman last week. 
“My hope is that we’ll be able to work very closely together and ensure that our people in the field get what they need to be able to do the job, and that we have a great relationship moving forward,” McDonnell said.
Asked for comment, Raman’s staff put out a short noncommittal statement. Raman will assure “the city is fully prepared to keep everyone safe during the Olympics,” the statement said, “regardless of leadership.” 
The task of securing the Games — from street-level violence to new threats like drones and cyberwarfare — has loomed large since L.A. accepted a bid to host the Olympics about a decade ago.
Within Los Angeles County alone, athletic venues will stretch from the San Fernando Valley to Venice, Long Beach and downtown Los Angeles. Also hosting sports: Orange County, with indoor volleyball; a half-dozen American cities, outside Southern California, with soccer; and Oklahoma City, which will be home to softball and canoe slalom.
The organizers of the Games and L.A. officials have been counting on financial aid from the federal government to cover all that territory. The $1 billion allocation arrived in President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
But California elected officials have been saying for months that they think more money will be needed. Planners expect to deploy as many as 16,000 police officers at a time across the broad Olympic region. They will be drawn from a larger pool of as many as 30,000 officers, who will stream into Southern California from dozens of other places.
McDonnell said it will take 9,400 officers a day during the busiest parts of the Olympic schedule just to protect competition venues. The LAPD plans to provide one-quarter to one-third of those officers, while outside agencies provide the rest, McDonnell said.
“It’s going to cost a lot of money to be able to do what needs to be done to police the Games appropriately,” McDonnell said.
The chief said that the new Democratic-controlled Congress due to be seated in January may provide more support to solidly blue California for the Olympics.
“It’s going to probably be good for L.A. because there is such a strong Democrat party representation here,” McDonnell said. “I think we will be able to make our pitch and hopefully be able to be heard and to be able to get the resources necessary to do the best job we can.”

title: What Is Bitcoin's Power Law and Why Are Analysts Concerned About $62K Support?
description:
Bitcoin's Power Law support line sits near $62K, says Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer. See why analysts are watching closely.
The post What Is Bitcoin's Power Law and Why Are Analysts Concerned About $62K Support? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Bitcoin (BTC) has returned to the support line of Bitcoin’s Power Law, says Fidelity Investments’ Jurrien Timmer. A fall well below that line, now near $62,000 and rising, would challenge his entire model.

However, Timmer stays bullish, citing the four-year cycle. For BTC holders, the retest asks whether cycle-based models still work as global liquidity recedes.

What Is Bitcoin’s Power Law, and Why Does Its Support Line Matter?

Bitcoin’s Power Law plots price against time on a logarithmic chart. Fidelity’s version adds a trendline and a lower support line.

On Timmer’s chart, the 2015 low of $230 landed below the line’s $252 reading. In contrast, the 2018 trough of $3,204 held above its $2,521 mark.

Timmer addressed the retest directly.

“I remain bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math, but it’s a bit disheartening that we are back again sitting on that power law support curve.”

Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity Investments.

Is Bitcoin’s Power Law Floor Holding as Liquidity Drains?

The same note ties Bitcoin’s weakness to receding global liquidity and fading risk appetite as the AI theme corrects. Bitcoin has also moved more in step with the S&P 500 lately, which Timmer reads as speculative-asset behavior.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt shared the chart on X. Brandt has separately asked whether his own weekly chart shows a head-and-shoulders top, a formation that can precede a decline.

In contrast, James Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, read that chart as a bullish inverse pattern. He said a drop below $57,000 would prove him wrong.

Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) lost about $2.35 billion in two weeks, and three bearish signals persist.

A break well below the line could shift the debate from cycle bottoms to whether cycles still apply. Cycle-based forecasts for Bitcoin’s record-high timeline could face the same test.

title: Why Blue-Chip NFTs Like Lil Pudgys and Azuki Are Trending While Crypto Crashes
description:
A basket of blue-chip NFTs is climbing while the tokens around it bleed. CoinGecko’s trending NFT data showed Lil Pudgys up 9.08% on the day, Azuki up 8.06%, CryptoPunks up
The post Why Blue-Chip NFTs Like Lil Pudgys and Azuki Are Trending While Crypto Crashes appeared first on NFT Plazas.
fullContent:
A basket of blue-chip NFTs is climbing while the tokens around it bleed. CoinGecko’s trending NFT data showed Lil Pudgys up 9.08% on the day, Azuki up 8.06%, CryptoPunks up 4.84%, Pudgy Penguins up 4.14% and Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC) up 3.87% in 24-hour floor price.

The backdrop could hardly be worse. Bitcoin slipped below $65,000 and Ether hovered near $1,800 on Wednesday, after a week in which Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan said BTC lost 12% and ETH 14% on a U.S. rate shock. CoinGecko’s Fear & Greed gauge reads Extreme Fear. Yet the oldest, most recognizable NFT collections are quietly moving the other way.

Five blue chips up, three majors down

All five trending collections gained in the same 24 hours that BTC and ETH fell, according to CoinGecko’s trending feed earlier Wednesday. The latest CoinGecko readings show those daily moves cooling to low single digits, with floors still near the levels below.

Collection 24h floor change (trending feed) Latest floor (ETH) Latest floor (USD, approx.) 24h sales
Lil Pudgys +9.08% 0.22 $397 11
Azuki +8.06% 0.48 $869 10
CryptoPunks +4.84% 28.24 $51,140 —
Pudgy Penguins +4.14% 2.39 $4,330 11
MAYC +3.87% 0.88 $1,587 24

On the token side, Bitcoin fell about 1% to $64,694 and Ether about 1.3% to roughly $1,808, per CoinGecko-based reports. Solana bounced around 3% on the day to near $75, but that follows a week in which SOL, like ETH, lost about 22%. Total crypto market value sits near $2.28 trillion.

The NFT sector is far smaller. CoinGecko puts global NFT market cap at about $1.21 billion, with only $1.42 million in 24-hour volume.

Bitcoin (BTC) Price Performance on Nov 18, 2026 (Source: CoinGecko)

Why the basket is breaking from tokens

Three forces explain most of the split: thin order books, ETH-priced floors and a rotation toward established brands.

Thin books move fast. Pudgy Penguins logged 11 sales in 24 hours and Azuki just 10. When sellers pull listings instead of dumping into a falling market, a handful of buyers can lift the cheapest ask several percent. Fungible tokens, by contrast, trade billions a day and absorb every macro headline instantly.

Floors are quoted in ETH. A floor that rises in ETH while ETH drops is partly a currency effect. Sellers who think in dollars raise their ETH asks to defend value, and buyers holding ETH find blue chips cheap in their own unit. Either way, the floor ticks up even when demand barely changes.

Money is rotating into names with history. CryptoSlam data reported by TokenPost shows weekly NFT sales rose 6.13% to $35.11 million in the week to November 17, even as transactions fell 6%. CryptoPunks sales jumped 252% to $1.21 million in that window. Fewer trades, bigger tickets and concentration in marquee collections point to collectors buying quality, not chasing mints.

The IP plays have real-world news

The leaders of this move are brands that sell things off-chain, and each has a fresh headline.

Pudgy Penguins and Lil Pudgys. A PSA 10 Pudgy Penguins Vibes card is listed in eBay-owned Goldin’s Fall TCG Elite Auction, beside Pokémon lots, with extended bidding from November 30. Pudgy products also reached 330 Kung Fu Tea locations this month, adding to plush lines in roughly 2,000 Walmart and 1,800-plus Target stores. Pudgy NFT sales rose 71% week on week to $588,280 in the period to November 14, while the wider NFT market slipped. Lil Pudgys, a 22,222-piece companion set to the 8,888 originals, offers the cheapest entry into that brand at about 0.22 ETH, which helps explain why it led the basket.

The contrast with the brand’s token is stark. PENGU fell nearly 21% in seven days to about $0.005. Holders appear to prefer the NFT, which carries IP licensing upside, over a token whose terms say it has no claim on company revenue.

Azuki. Chiru Labs now calls Azuki an IP company built around a trading card game and a manga. Its second card set, Fractured Domains (AZK-02), is due in stores on November 20, giving traders a dated catalyst two days out.

CryptoPunks and MAYC. Punks remain the sector’s reserve asset, holding about 42% of NFT market-cap dominance on CoinGecko. MAYC, at under 1 ETH, is the cheapest route into the Yuga Labs ape ecosystem and recorded the most sales of the five, at 24.

Why the rally may not stick

The same thin liquidity that lifts floors can sink them just as quickly. With the whole NFT market trading about $1.42 million in 24 hours, a single motivated seller could erase a day’s gains.

The dollar math is also less impressive than the ETH math. A 4% floor gain on CryptoPunks roughly offsets one day of ETH weakness; it does not undo ETH’s 14% slide last week. In USD terms, most of these collections remain far below their 2021–22 peaks; Azuki once floored near 30 ETH.

Macro risk has not cleared. Hougan tied last week’s sell-off to a hotter-than-expected U.S. CPI print, a jump in two-year Treasury yields and about $2 billion in weekend leveraged liquidations, and analysts now point to the December Fed decision as the next test. Pudgy’s ecosystem faces its own friction too: the Abstract chain it backed is set to shut down on December 15.

What to watch next

The next two weeks will show whether blue chips are a refuge or just a pocket of illiquidity. Four markers matter:

  • November 20: Azuki’s Fractured Domains card set lands in stores; watch whether the floor holds after the event.
  • November 30: extended bidding opens on the Pudgy Penguins card at Goldin, a test of crossover demand from traditional collectors.
  • ETH near $1,750: Tuesday’s intraday low. A break lower would pressure ETH-priced floors from both sides.
  • Weekly CryptoSlam sales: a second week of rising dollar volume with concentration in blue chips would confirm rotation rather than noise.

For now, the signal is narrow but clear. In a market gripped by fear, collectors are paying up for NFTs with brands, products and years of history, not for the tokens that trade beside them.

title: Data Infrastructure Behind Live Sports Prediction Markets is Coming Under Scrutiny
description: Monthly trading volume on top prediction markets has frequently crossed $50B during major global sports tournaments like FIFA World Cup and NBA league.
fullContent:
Monthly trading volume on top prediction markets has frequently crossed $50B during major global sports tournaments like FIFA World Cup and NBA league. Platforms like Polymarket and Kalshi have attracted bettors from around the world by offering unique markets that are often missing on traditional gambling websites. Prediction markets let bettors to wager on more than just the winner or the loser of a particular match. For example, in a UFC bout there could be a market around “Will the first strike thrown in the match be a leg kick?”. These markets are more volatile and resolve is milliseconds. During the last FIFA world cup, Polymarket hosted an $89.2 million market on whether Cristiano Ronaldo would visibly cry during a match. 

These dynamic contracts have created a need for a data provider that supplies prediction markets with continuous verifiable and accurate sports data. Since those platforms use smart contracts to settle markets, the challenge of sourcing data is subtly different from traditional sports betting websites where the feed and sportsbooks are centralized and what goes on behind the scenes is not visible to the end users. Smart contracts operate on-chain and can not directly access information from the outside world, including live-scores, match events, or player statistics. They rely on outside data suppliers, known as Oracles, to bring the data on blockchain. These oracles act as a link between real life events and on-chain applications, allowing smart contracts to use that data to settle markets. 

From Sports Data Feeds to On-Chain Verification

Traditional sports data providers have spent decades building infrastructure to supply live scores, odds and match statistics to broadcasters, betting platforms and other centralized systems. For developers building on-chain prediction markets, however, accessing the same quality and depth of real-time sports data has not always been straightforward.

As markets get settled based on predefined conditions through smart contracts automatically, prediction market platforms need an extra layer of verification to establish that the data used to settle an outcome has not been altered or manipulated along the way. 

TxLINE opens up TxODDS' established sports data infrastructure to blockchain developers, allowing them to integrate professional-grade sports feeds directly into their prediction market applications. Through TxODDS' existing APIs and streaming feeds, developers can access live odds, scores and match statistics without having to build and maintain their own data collection and distribution infrastructure. TxLINE also addresses a data verification challenge specific to on-chain applications. When smart contracts automatically settle markets based on match results and predefined conditions, developers need confidence that the information triggering those settlements is accurate and has not been manipulated. TxLINE combines traditional data delivery with cryptographic proofs and timestamped on-chain records on Solana, giving developers a way to independently verify the integrity and origin of the data they receive.

In effect, TxLINE bridges two infrastructure layers that have largely operated separately: established sports data distribution and blockchain-based verification.

Verifying Live Data at Scale 

Delivering accurate data within milliseconds through an API and proving the integrity of that data are two different things. Developers need to be able to verify that data provided matches with what the provider originally published and the time record of when it was published. TxODDS has been supplying sports data to the betting industry since 1999, feeding sportsbooks and prediction markets/platforms worldwide. Its infrastructure delivers live odds updates in as little as 8–10 milliseconds, alongside live scores and match statistics, powering sportsbooks and other betting platforms worldwide.

TxODDS has specifically designed TxLINE as a solution to supplying verifiable sports data on Solana to prediction markets. TxLINE uses the TxODDS’ existing live sports-data feeds and combines with cryptographic verification and on-chain data recording on Solana blockchain. TxODDS CEO Einar Knobel explained, “TxLINE approaches this problem by combining traditional data distribution with on-chain based verification. Live scores, odds and match statistics continue to reach developers through Tx APIs and streaming feeds, while the verification process happens separately.

He added, “TxLINE groups data records into batches and uses Merkle trees to generate cryptographic proofs of their integrity. Instead of putting every update on-chain, it records the resulting Merkle root on Solana, which creates a timestamped reference that can be used to check individual records against the original data batch.”

The result is a system that allows prediction-market developers to independently verify the authenticity and timing of sports data without having to put every live update on-chain. By separating high-speed data delivery from cryptographic verification, TxLINE aims to bring the transparency and auditability of blockchain infrastructure to the speed-sensitive world of sports prediction markets.

Prediction Markets Face Growing Demands for Data Integrity

The regulatory treatment of sports contracts within the prediction markets are also influencing how the infrastructure behind these markets should be built. US CFTC has proposed to include sports events on prediction markets within its definition of swaps, bringing them under its derivatives regulatory framework. The regulatory agency has also signed an MoU with NBA and other major sports organisations to share information and coordinate on protecting the integrity of professional sports when it comes to prediction markets. 

Prediction markets are placing new demands on the systems responsible for delivering and verifying market data. As these markets grow, settlement processes, trading surveillance and the integrity of the underlying data will face higher scrutiny

Platforms will need to prove that the data that is being used to settle contracts comes from reliable sources and can be independently checked, particularly as regulators and sports organisations pay closer attention to how these markets operate. For TxODDS, TxLINE represents an attempt to address this emerging requirement by bringing an established sports-data distribution infrastructure into on-chain applications.

title: DBS Taps Circle’s USDC Infrastructure to Push Institutional Stablecoin Adoption in Asia
description: The partnership gives eligible DBS clients a direct way to mint and redeem USDC, thereby reducing reliance on secondary market liquidity.
fullContent:
Circle has partnered with Singapore’s largest bank, DBS, to expand institutional access to USDC in Asia, allowing eligible clients of the bank to mint and redeem the stablecoin directly while settling USD-USDC transactions around the clock.

The arrangement gives institutions another option for sourcing USDC and reduces their reliance on secondary market liquidity.

DBS-Circle Partnership

According to the official blog post, clients will also be able to convert between USD and the stablecoin outside conventional banking hours, with 24/7 settlement available through DBS for minting and redemption.

The companies are targeting institutions that use stablecoins for treasury operations, payments, settlement and liquidity management. With traditional banking services often tied to operating hours and cut-off times, round-the-clock settlement offers institutions more flexibility when moving funds between fiat and digital asset markets, Circle said.

The partnership comes as corporations increasingly explore tokenized money for financial operations. DBS cited its The Great Rewiring: Money in a new order report, which found that 88% of large corporations were already deploying or piloting tokenized money use cases. More than three in five were also adopting stablecoins or planning to introduce them.

Besides, DBS and Circle are also involved in Project BLOOM, an initiative led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) focused on making tokenized money work safely and at scale. Their participation includes efforts to improve interoperability between tokenized money and different financial networks, as the project looks to make digital money easier to use across financial systems.

Commenting on the development, Evy Theunis, Head of Digital Assets, Institutional Banking Group, DBS, explained that institutions are increasingly turning to tokenized money to manage funds more easily and expand into new markets. She went on to add,

“This partnership meets that demand by bringing together Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure and global reach with DBS’ trusted banking, liquidity and digital asset capabilities in Asia. We believe the future of financial services will be multi-modal and multi-instrumental, with different forms of tokenized money serving different needs.”

Major Milestones

Last month, USDC became the first stablecoin in the EU to receive significant e-money token status under MiCA, bringing it under direct EBA supervision with tighter oversight of reserves, liquidity, as well as capital requirements.

In September, Binance invested $100 million in Circle, buying over 1.23 million shares, while signing a fresh five-year deal to expand USDC adoption and strengthen its presence across global crypto markets.

title: NGINX2Root: Five nginx Flaws, Led by CVE-2026-123007. How to Find, Mitigate, and Patch Now
description: Executive Summary NGINX2Root is a set of five nginx vulnerabilities disclosed on November 18, 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in the way nginx handles HTTP/2 connections. F5, which maintains nginx, rates it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can crash nginx worker […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

NGINX2Root is a set of five nginx vulnerabilities disclosed on November 18, 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in the way nginx handles HTTP/2 connections. F5, which maintains nginx, rates it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can crash nginx worker processes, and researchers have demonstrated remote code execution with the privileges of the nginx worker. Where the worker runs without root privileges, an attacker would need an additional escalation path to gain root. This could involve chaining the NGINX vulnerability with a suitable local privilege-escalation flaw.

Unpatched builds of NGINX Open Source from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, and unpatched NGINX Plus builds, are in scope when HTTP/2 is enabled. Fixes shipped in NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and turning off HTTP/2 closes this exposure where patching has to wait. A separate Linux kernel flaw that the researchers used to go from the worker account to root has no patch yet. Start with internet-facing nginx servers that accept HTTP/2, and assign an owner and a deadline to every system still unpatched.

What’s at Risk

A Flaw in nginx Could Hand Attackers the Front Door to Your Applications. nginx is often the first system a web request reaches. It runs as a web server, a reverse proxy (a server that passes requests to the applications behind it), a load balancer, and the entry point to Kubernetes clusters. CVE-2026-123007 is in nginx’s own HTTP/2 code, so no application behind it has to be at fault.

HTTP/2 lets a client tell the server how much data it is allowed to send. nginx can lose count of that allowance when a client cancels requests at the right moment. The bad count later makes nginx copy memory it should not touch.

F5 says the result is typically a crash of the nginx worker, the process that handles live traffic. F5 also says code execution is possible where ASLR, the memory-address randomization that makes exploits harder, is disabled or bypassed. Xint, the team that named NGINX2Root, reports doing exactly that: it leaked memory addresses and then ran commands as the nginx worker over a public HTTPS port.

In Qualys TRU’s assessment, three outcomes matter to the business:

  • Exposure of traffic and keys. Code running in the worker can read requests and responses after nginx decrypts them, including passwords and session tokens. It may also expose TLS private keys that are held in software and accessible to the worker.
  • A foothold behind the perimeter. Backend systems usually trust the proxy in front of them. An attacker on that proxy starts from a trusted position.
  • Outages. A failed attempt can still crash workers and drop connections.

Workers normally run under a restricted account. An attacker gets whatever privileges the worker actually has, so if it already runs as root, no further escalation is needed in that environment. Where it does not, the researchers chained a separate flaw in the Linux kernel’s SCTP code to get root. SCTP is a network protocol, like TCP, that the kernel supports. They report root on the host, including from nginx running inside a Docker container. That kernel flaw has no CVE and no patch yet, so patching nginx removes the remote entry point but not the step to root.

NGINX2Root covers four more nginx flaws. F5 scores all five 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1, and the same nginx releases fix them. Each needs a different configuration:

The rest of this post focuses on CVE-2026-123007, the flaw with the widest reach.

Are You Affected?

A system is in scope only when both conditions are true. For an attack to work, the attacker must also be able to open an HTTP/2 connection to nginx itself.

F5 notes that it did not evaluate versions past End of Technical Support. F5 also lists BIG-IP, BIG-IQ, and F5OS as not vulnerable in its advisory.

The checks below come from the researchers’ write-up. Run them on the nginx host. The first shows whether the build includes HTTP/2. The second shows whether the configuration turns it on.

nginx -V 2>&1 | grep -o — ‘–with-http_v2_module’

sudo nginx -T 2>&1 | sed ‘s/#.*//’ | grep -nE ‘listen[[:space:]].*http2|^[[:space:]]*http2[[:space:]]+on[[:space:]]*;’

Run this one from outside your network. ALPN protocol: h2 means the server accepts HTTP/2 from the internet.

openssl s_client -connect HOST:443 -servername HOST -alpn h2 </dev/null 2>&1 | grep -E ‘ALPN protocol:|No ALPN negotiated’

nginx also ships inside other software. Status as of November 18, 2026:

Three cautions when scoping:

  • Do not rely on nginx -v alone. Distributions often fix a flaw without changing the nginx version number. Compare the full package version with the distribution’s advisory.
  • Check where the HTTP/2 connection ends. If a CDN or load balancer handles HTTP/2 in front of nginx, an outside test only reaches that device. Test the nginx port directly.
  • Use internet exposure to order the work, not to close findings. An internal nginx with HTTP/2 on is still reachable by an attacker who is already inside the network.

Exploitation Status

As of November 18, 2026, we have not seen public confirmation of exploitation in the wild.

Working exploit code is public. The team behind NGINX2Root also reports its own exploit working over public IP addresses on AWS, GCP, and Azure, and is holding back the final steps.

The public exploit is hard to use. It sends a very large number of HTTP/2 control messages over one long-lived connection for several minutes, has to reach nginx directly, and depends on a specific memory-copy routine in the standard Linux C library on 64-bit Intel and AMD processors.

These limits slow mass exploitation. In Qualys TRU’s assessment, they do not protect a specific internet-facing server from a capable attacker, and other techniques may follow.

What to Do Now

Updating nginx is the only complete fix. F5 released fixed builds on November 18, 2026.

Linux distributions publish on their own schedules. As of November 18, 2026, Ubuntu and Debian had not shipped fixed packages. Use your vendor’s advisory to identify the fixed package and confirm it addresses CVE-2026-123007.

Restart nginx after you update. A reload applies configuration changes but keeps the old program running, so the flaw stays in memory until a restart.

If you cannot patch today, turn off HTTP/2 on every affected listener. F5 states the flaw affects only configurations that use HTTP/2, and the researchers recommend this as a temporary measure. For the exact steps, see nginx’s documentation for the http2 directive, CERT-EU’s advisory, and section 3.3 of the researchers’ write-up. Clients fall back to HTTP/1.1. Services that need HTTP/2, such as gRPC, will stop working, so test first. This covers CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 only, and it does not replace the patch.

Advice for Risk and Vulnerability Management Teams

Qualys TRU’s advice for the teams running this response:

  • Do not let the score set the deadline: Under CVSS v3.1 this flaw is 8.1, which many remediation policies file as High. Public exploit code and a server that faces the internet matter more than the number. Handle vulnerable nginx deployments with externally reachable HTTP/2 as an emergency.
  • Close findings on evidence: A server is done when the fixed build is installed, nginx has been restarted, and the vendor’s advisory confirms the package covers all five CVEs. Report patched, temporarily mitigated, not exposed by configuration, and unknown as separate states, and do not count unknown as safe.
  • Fix the template as well as the server: Update container images, Helm charts, machine images, and autoscaling templates. Otherwise the next scale-out or failover brings the vulnerable build back.
  • Put an end date on every workaround: Turning off HTTP/2 covers two of the five flaws, and the next configuration push can undo it. Record who owns each exception and when it ends.
  • Decide what to do with nginx that will not get a fix: The community ingress-nginx project is archived, and the older NGINX Plus R-series branches have no fixed build listed, although fixed NGINX Plus 37.x releases exist. These need a migration plan or a signed risk acceptance.
  • Treat privilege escalation flaws as part of this response: Where the worker runs without root privileges, an attacker would need an additional escalation path to gain root. The newly disclosed SCTP flaw is one such path, and any other local privilege-escalation flaw that can be exploited from the worker’s context could serve the same purpose. Patch known local privilege-escalation flaws on nginx hosts, in the kernel and elsewhere, with the same urgency. A current kernel does not mean the SCTP flaw is fixed, because that flaw has no patch yet.

How Qualys Can Help

Inventory nginx Installations with Qualys CSAM

Qualys CyberSecurity Asset Management (CSAM) lists every asset with nginx installed, along with the version of each installation, so teams can quickly scope NGINX2Root remediation. Because NGINX Open Source 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 is affected, the version tells you which installations are in range. It does not tell you whether HTTP/2 is turned on or whether a Linux distribution has backported the fix, so check those separately. nginx bundled in containers, Kubernetes ingress controllers, and appliances may not appear in a standard inventory, so check those separately too.

Assets With nginx in the Affected Range

Use the following CSAM query to identify potentially affected NGINX Open Source installations on the stable, mainline, and older branches for further assessment. It uses two ranges because 1.31.0 through 1.31.8 are affected even though they are higher than the fixed 1.30.7.

software:(name:”nginx” AND ( (version>=1.9.5 AND version<1.30.7) OR (version>=1.31.0 AND version<1.31.9) ))

Detection VMDR QIDs

Qualys is releasing the following detection QIDs. We will add distribution-specific detection QIDs to this blog as they are released.

title: Satoshi Nakamoto’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Reveals a 2014 Mystery
description:
Just weeks after the Bitcoin whitepaper turned 18, a forgotten forum created by Satoshi Nakamoto is drawing fresh attention. A post on X has sparked a lively debate about it. Its admin account logged in again in 2014. That detail deepens the long mystery around Bitcoin’s anonymous creator. How Satoshi’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Drew Attention
The post Satoshi Nakamoto’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Reveals a 2014 Mystery appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Just weeks after the Bitcoin whitepaper turned 18, a forgotten forum created by Satoshi Nakamoto is drawing fresh attention. A post on X has sparked a lively debate about it.

Its admin account logged in again in 2014. That detail deepens the long mystery around Bitcoin’s anonymous creator.

How Satoshi’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Drew Attention

ZetaBoards was a free service that let anyone launch an online forum. In November 2009, Satoshi used it to create a board simply called Bitcoin.

At the time, Bitcoin was barely a year old. Satoshi had published the whitepaper on October 31, 2008, and was now searching for a home for its tiny community.

However, this forum never became the main hub.

Days later, Satoshi opened a forum on bitcoin.org, which later became BitcoinTalk.

The forum drew attention after crypto enthusiast Sean Murray shared an archived copy of the page on X. His post quickly sparked debate. The Wayback Machine had saved that snapshot in June 2018.

The snapshot shows just three members, and each held administrator rights. The “satoshi” account joined on November 13, 2009, and left five posts. It was last active on November 21, 2009.

Meanwhile, “sirius-m” registered on November 15 but never posted. The third account, “admin,” joined on November 14, 2009. Surprisingly, it last logged in on June 17, 2014.

Who Logged Into Satoshi’s Forum in 2014?

Murray offered a partial answer. He shared a November 14, 2009 email from Satoshi to Martti Malmi, one of Bitcoin’s earliest developers.

In it, Satoshi explained that InvisionFree was moving to ZetaBoards, so he had set up a forum there. He then sent Malmi the admin login and password.

The dates match perfectly. The admin account appeared the same day as the email, and Malmi has long used the “sirius-m” nickname. Still, at least two people knew the admin password.

As a result, nobody can say for sure who logged in back in 2014.

That uncertainty fits a much larger puzzle. Eighteen years after the whitepaper, Satoshi’s identity remains unknown. Over time, theories have pointed to cypherpunks such as Hal Finney, Nick Szabo, and Adam Back.

In 2024, the HBO documentary Money Electric suggested developer Peter Todd, who denied the claim. That same year, a UK court ruled that Craig Wright is not Satoshi.

Now, another twist has emerged. Charlie Shrem, an early Bitcoin entrepreneur, recently claimed that researchers traced Satoshi through several fictional names.

According to Shrem, Satoshi never left the community and kept talking under other pseudonyms.

However, the group does not plan to reveal his identity.

The post Satoshi Nakamoto’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Reveals a 2014 Mystery appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Will Bitcoin Rise Again? 3 Factors Why Selling Pressure May Be Fading
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) could be approaching a turning point as selling pressure from miners and whales fades, potentially setting the stage for a recovery.
In an interview with Anthony Pompliano, Lava founder and CEO Shehzan Maredia identified three developments that could strengthen Bitcoin’s long-term outlook:

Reduced selling pressure: Miners and whales may have already completed much of their selling as indicated by Bitcoin’s muted reaction to a recent major crypto exchange hack.
Retail accumulation: Long-term holders continue buying Bitcoin despite falling prices.
International adoption: Stablecoin payments are introducing new users to Bitcoin as a savings asset.
He also downplayed the importance of the Clarity Act for Bitcoin, arguing that long-term prospects depend more on adoption, security and savings demand than additional market-structure legislation.
Could AI Profits Trigger Next Rally?
Maredia expects investors to rotate profits from AI investments into Bitcoin, particularly as equity valuations remain stretched.
He suggested that the Democratic election sweep could increase regulatory pressure on AI, potentially accelerating capital flows into Bitcoin.
While he does not expect another tenfold rally within a year, Maredia sees Bitcoin maturing into a long-term asset with steadier returns and lower volatility.
He added that Bitcoin’s halving cycle remains relevant, but investor demand and market structure will increasingly drive prices.

title: Is the AI party over? Anthropic is about to find out.
description:
Thursday is supposed to be a celebration of AI.
Anthropic (ANT) is heading toward its long-awaited IPO at the Nasdaq, potentially giving Wall Street one of the biggest new pure-play AI investment stories in years. 
Before you hit me up on X, Elon Musk-led SpaceX (SPCX) is not a pure-play AI company. It's an industrial company with a whole lot of AI bolted on.
But there's a problem amid all the Anthropic IPO hoopla.
The very stocks that fueled this AI boom are still under pressure. Just look at the sell-offs this week in top tech names like CoreWeave (CRWV), Salesforce (CRM), and even AMD (AMD).
Read more: Follow along for live updates on the Anthropic IPO
Investors are questioning the AI spending, the valuations, the financing arrangements — and whether the returns will ever justify the billions being poured into this technology.
And the timing couldn't be more fascinating.
Truist chief market strategist Keith Lerner noted that tech valuations have fallen 42% over the past year. The sector has gone from outperforming the S&P 500 (^GSPC) by 25% over six months to underperforming it by 6%. Bank of America's latest fund manager survey shows investors have cut tech exposure by the most since June 2006.
That's a serious reset.
The question pre-Anthropic IPO: Is Wall Street finally getting too negative?
The AI build-out isn't disappearing, as we saw from Nvidia (NVDA) on Tuesday. Companies are still spending. The technology is still evolving. And as Lerner pointed out, previous tech pullbacks of more than 10% during this bull market were followed by an average rebound of 47%.
That doesn't guarantee a repeat. There are real risks — and this AI stock sell-off could get worse.
Anthropic's IPO arrives at a moment when investors are suddenly asking what could go wrong with AI.
Maybe it's time to ask the other question: What could go right?
Investing in Anthropic is like investing in a young Amazon (AMZN), "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary told me on Sozzi Unleashed. Valid point.
Indeed, the biggest opportunity in tech may emerge when Wall Street least wants to own it.
That's the trade I'm watching. Well, that and the first few ticks in ticker symbol ANT!
Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks at the Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco on Sept. 15, 2026. (Reuters/Carlos Barria)

title: Republicans want Trump to confront Xi over 2 Americans accused of spying
description:
By Simon Lewis and Jonathan Landay 
   WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Republican lawmakers on Wednesday urged President Donald Trump to again press Chinese leader Xi Jinping to free two Americans designated as wrongfully detained, ‌as well as political prisoners, when the two meet in Shenzhen on Thursday. 
   Advocates for the ‌Americans, Youlin Chen and Min Zin, say they expect Trump to raise their cases with Xi. 
   John Moolenaar, chairman of the House Select Committee ​on China, Robert Aderholt, chairman of the House Values Action Team, and Chris Smith, co-chairman of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China, issued the statement. Seventeen other House Republicans co-signed it. 
   The lawmakers said the two men were held on "baseless suspicions" of endangering national security. They cited the July release of Pastor Ezra Jin as an example of ‌diplomacy producing results and called for other ⁠detainees, including Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai and Uyghur economist Ilham Tohti, to be freed. 
   “They should all be released immediately,” the lawmakers said. 
   Responding to the statement, a ⁠US official said, “Resolving the wrongful detentions of US citizens is always a top priority for the president.” 
   The wrongfully detained designation makes the pair's release a top US priority. 
   US officials and advocates for the detained pair say China has not ​engaged on ​the cases, despite Trump raising Chen's case at a ​meeting with Xi in May and both men's cases ‌in September. 
   A Chinese Embassy spokesperson said: "China is a country governed by the rule of law. Its judicial authorities handle cases in accordance with the law, and there is no such thing as so-called wrongful detention." 
   Min Zin, a researcher on Myanmar, was detained during a visit to southwest China in June. China’s Foreign Ministry said the American citizen was suspected of spying and endangering Chinese national security. 
   Chen is a Chinese-born seismologist whose published work ‌on the seismographic signatures of North Korean nuclear tests was ​US-funded. He was arrested at Beijing's international airport on November 5, ​2024, as he prepared to fly home. ​Chinese authorities charged him with espionage on May 1, 2025. 
   Secretary of State Marco Rubio ‌has designated both men as wrongfully detained. 
   The State ​Department last month added a "D" ​indicator to its China travel advisory, warning of the risk of wrongful detention. It could raise the risk level of its travel advisory for China if progress is not made. 
   Eric Lebson, chief strategy ​officer of Global Reach, an advocacy ‌group working with Chen’s family, said it was "uncharacteristic of the Chinese government to not engage on ​resolving matters of this type after two discussions about them at the presidential level." 
   (Reporting by ​Simon Lewis and Jonathan Landay; Editing by Sonali Paul)

title: Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It
description:
Cybersecurity stocks surged on November 18 as investors bet on defense against AI hacking, a threat crypto knows.
The post Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Cybersecurity stocks were the standout of the November 18 session. The move echoes a September rally that Dow Jones tied to the debate over artificial intelligence (AI) risks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and CrowdStrike (CRWD) rose substantially as the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.13%. However, Palo Alto then reported earnings after the bell, and its shares fell on guidance.

Are Cybersecurity Stocks Pricing In AI Fear?

Yahoo Finance’s top U.S. gainers list on November 19 showed 15 of 25 names were security or network infrastructure firms.

Palo Alto reported that next-generation security annual recurring revenue jumped 66% to $9.73 billion. It raised full-year profit guidance, yet shares still fell afterward.

The company also authorized a $1 billion buyback through 2027, equal to 0.36% of its market value.

Palo Alto also announced plans to acquire Applied Compute. The deal targets secure open-weight AI models, which publish their trained parameters, for enterprise customers.

Palo Alto chief executive Nikesh Arora said in September that awareness of weaponized AI is growing. Dow Jones reported that OpenAI models breached Hugging Face, an AI company, adding urgency to the debate.

Results from other security vendors could show how much of the rally reflects AI fear rather than earnings.

Has Crypto Already Felt the Threat?

April 2026 crypto hacks drained more than $606 million from protocols in the first 18 days of the month. That made it the worst month for exploits since February 2025.

Whether AI drove those losses, however, remains contested. Wasabi Protocol, a Decentralized Finance (DeFi) platform, lost over $5 million to an admin-key compromise.

The AI-driven DeFi hacker theory resurfaced, though on-chain security firm Blockaid traced the breach to one admin wallet.

Drift Protocol and KelpDAO, the two biggest April hacks, totaled $577 million. Neither was a code exploit, according to a review of 2026 DeFi losses.

Meanwhile, equity investors bid up security stocks while crypto still debates whether AI is behind its losses. DeFi total value locked, the capital deposited in protocols, had fallen 39% in 2026 by late June.

The post Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Anthropic Prices IPO At $83, Above Range, In What Could Be Biggest Listing Ever (UPDATED)
description:
Editor’s note: This story has been updated with Anthropic’s $83-per-share IPO price; an earlier version reported only the expected price range.
Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the $70-to-$78 range it marketed to investors, according to people familiar with the matter cited by CNBC and Bloomberg, a day before the stock is set to make its highly anticipated Nasdaq debut.
With the higher price, the IPO is expected to raise at least $68 billion, Bloomberg reported. 
CNBC said that if all 825 million shares originally planned are sold, the offering would bring in about $68.5 billion. Adding the $26 billion that investors including Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) agreed to invest at the IPO price, the total would come to more than $94 billion, the largest IPO on record.
That would top SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June with its base IPO offering, or $86.2 billion including the over-allotment option. 
Anthropic had marketed a base offering of 801.4 million shares, while selling investors offered 23.6 million shares, according to its filings. Bloomberg reported the size of the offering has increased, which could lift the final total. 
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE:GS) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) are leading the offering, with 20 other banks participating. Shares are expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, making Anthropic the first frontier AI lab to go public — ahead of rival OpenAI, which isn’t planning a listing before 2027.
Wall Street Sees The Listing As A Catalyst
At HSBC, the deal is framed as a possible turning point for a battered tech trade. Analysts still read it that way after a week in which Nvidia was hit by the departure of Jensen Huang.
“The upcoming Anthropic IPO is the likely next positive catalyst for equities, in our view,” Max Kettner, HSBC’s chief multi-asset strategist, wrote in a Monday note.
“This week’s Anthropic IPO could well be the next bullish catalyst for tech given likely more reasonable valuations,” the note added. 
It also warned that “it’s very unlikely that even a successful IPO will finally lead to a more ‘trending’ market.”
At $83, Anthropic lists below Morningstar‘s fair value estimate of $92 per share, or about $1.7 trillion. 
That estimate assumes 47% annual revenue growth over five years. Morningstar’s bull case is $188 a share and its bear case is $25, with a “Very High” uncertainty rating.
Prediction Markets Are Scaling Back
Traders on Polymarket are lowering their expectations for the debut.
In the market on Anthropic’s closing market cap on its first trading day, the $1.25 trillion-to-$1.5 trillion bracket leads at 44.5%. That is up 6.5 percentage points in the past day. 
The odds of a close below $1.25 trillion have risen 18.9 points in a week, to 39.1%.
The odds of a close above $1.5 trillion have dropped to 19.9%, down 24.3 points in a week. The $1.75 trillion-to-$2 trillion bracket has fallen to 3.4%. The event has drawn more than $11.2 million in volume.




From $41 Million To $16 Billion In Three Years
The prospectus shows how fast revenue has grown.
Anthropic reported $41 million in revenue in 2023, its first commercial year. That rose to $386 million in 2024, up about 842%. In 2025, revenue reached $4.59 billion, an increase of about 1,088% from a year earlier.
Growth has not slowed in 2026. Revenue hit $16.3 billion in the first six months of the year, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. That is about 14 times as much, and about 3.5 times Anthropic’s revenue for all of 2025. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, revenue reached $33.24 billion, up roughly 1,200% from a year earlier, according to the prospectus.
The prospectus says revenue grew 1,368% year over year in the three months ended June 30, 2026, to about $11.6 billion. That was up 144% from the first quarter.
Compute and infrastructure expenses grew 300% over the same period. That gap between revenue growth and cost growth is the core of the bull case.
Customers Are Spending Much More
Anthropic says its net revenue retention was about 900% as of Sept. 30, 2026. In other words, existing customers spent roughly nine times more than a year earlier.
Customers generating more than $100,000 in trailing 12-month revenue rose to more than 11,900, up from about 950 a year earlier.
The losses are also large. Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, compared with about $42 billion for all of 2025.
That leaves the question Wall Street will start answering Thursday. Investors can see the growth in the numbers. What they are paying $83 a share for is how long it lasts.

title: S&P 500 Breaks Critical Support: Is a Bigger Stock Market Crash Coming?
description:
The S&P 500 lost its 200-day moving average. Historical data, hedging, and key chart levels hint at what comes next.
The post S&P 500 Breaks Critical Support: Is a Bigger Stock Market Crash Coming? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
The S&P 500 has fallen below one of Wall Street’s most closely watched warning levels, raising fears that the stock market correction could deepen.

The index dropped to 7,323 on Tuesday, closing below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 7. It is now 6.4% below October’s record high.

Even Nvidia’s stronger-than-expected earnings have failed to settle the bigger concern: whether the AI-driven stock market rally is losing momentum.

History Suggests the S&P 500 Could Fall Further

Market research firm Bluekurtic found a troubling historical pattern.

Although the S&P 500 closed below its 200-day average, the SPY ETF recovered enough to finish slightly above its own.

Since 1993, this has happened 11 times. In 10 cases, SPY fell further within the following 10 trading sessions. The average maximum decline was 4.2%.

“It feels premature to call today as a bottom in the S&P 500.”

However, the median 10-day return was just -0.3%, suggesting that previous selloffs often stabilized relatively quickly.

Another indicator, the Zweig Breadth Thrust, has entered an early setup phase. All 17 confirmed signals since 1950 preceded higher markets six and 12 months later.

However, fewer than 2% of setups become confirmed signals.

Traders Are Preparing for More Volatility

The Cboe one-day volatility index surged 35.7% to 26.84 on Tuesday, reflecting expectations of a roughly 1.7% market move in either direction.

Trader Klarck warns that weakening market participation is leaving the S&P 500 increasingly dependent on technology giants.

He believes Anthropic’s November 19 IPO could mark a peak in AI enthusiasm, although that remains speculative.

For investors, 7,345 is the immediate level to watch. Reclaiming that moving average could support a recovery. 

Further weakness would put the 7,240 support area in focus, increasing the risk of a deeper correction.

title: $3 Million in Crypto, Gone Out of Reach, All Because of One Mistake
description: Two addresses flagged as scam-linked reportedly belong to Merlin Chain's bridge, which remains unlabeled in many blockchain compliance tools.
fullContent:
Blockchain investigator ZachXBT has accused Indian law enforcement of wrongly freezing approximately $3 million worth of BTC belonging to a Chinese crypto investor.

This is after they mistook transactions involving the Merlin Chain bridge for funds linked to a pig butchering scam.

Merlin Chain Bridge Mistaken for Scam-Linked Address

In an investigation published on November 18, ZachXBT traced the dispute to a May 2025 pig butchering case, where a victim identified as Andhra Pradesh allegedly lost $1.7 million in BTC, USDT, DOGE, and SOL.

The victim reported the incident to the criminal investigation department, which filed a charge sheet in March this year.

Then in July 2025, the Chinese investor, who goes by “Keym” on X, moved 15 BTC from an address, 3NcBhqK, to a deposit address on Gate, with the crypto exchange then freezing that account days later. At the time, it held about $3 million worth of crypto, although its remaining balance right now is worth around $1.5 million to $1.6 million because of declines in the value of the assets.

That freezing, according to ZachXBT, was due to a labeling error. He noted that shortly before the Gate deposit, a wallet controlled by Keym received funds from two addresses tagged as alibart[.]bit, which Indian police had identified as being associated with the scam that Pradesh had been a victim of.

However, per the analyst’s investigations, both addresses are part of the Merlin Chain bridge infrastructure, which most compliance tools often leave unlabeled.

According to the investigator, Keym is an ordinary user of Merlin, and transaction records tie three Merlin withdrawals between March and June 2025 to payouts from those bridge addresses, with the funds coming out of 50 BTC Keym bridged into Merlin on March 28, 2024. That’s more than a year before the alleged theft, and the analyst found no on-chain link to the victim’s losses.

Pressure on Exchanges and Police

On their part, Keym recounted how Gate had requested documentation shortly after their July 2025 deposit, but even after repeated submissions, the restriction on the account was not resolved. The user’s lawyers also reportedly requested transaction evidence connecting their holdings to the stolen funds, but apparently, investigators never provided the requested chain of transactions.

ZachXBT called the handling of the case “embarrassing incompetence,” adding that Indian law enforcement “seems incapable of reviewing basic blockchain data.”

“Indian LE, the prosecutor and the judge all signed off on this, Gate froze the account, and LE did a full press release about it recently, while the real victim here (the Gate user) hasn’t had access to his funds for nearly 16 months,” he wrote.

The sleuth has been busy, having earlier this month flagged a suspected theft of at least $133 million worth of crypto from several CEX accounts linked to French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa.

The post $3 Million in Crypto, Gone Out of Reach, All Because of One Mistake appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: Variational Hits $1.5B Valuation in $110M Round to Take on Robinhood and IBKR
description:
Crypto trading startup Variational raised $110 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in the Series B round to compete with brokerages like Robinhood Markets Inc. and Interactive Brokers LLC. 
The financing round was led by Bain Capital Crypto, an early-stage crypto-native fund, where Stefan Cohen is a partner.  Other participants included Dragonfly Capital, HSG and Peak XV. 
“They’re [Variational] basically plugging into all of these off-chain liquidity sources and innovating on this broker model that they’ve established,” said Stefan Cohen.
 Crypto Startup with Traditional Finance Ambitions 
Variational is a derivatives trading protocol registered in the Cayman Islands that lets users trade swaps and perpetuals for both crypto and traditional assets, including stocks, commodities and pre-IPO equities. 
The company reports over 100,000 accounts and more than $475 billion in trading volume processed since launching the trading platform in 2025. 
Variational operates on a brokerage model, routing trades to and from crypto protocols and centralised trading venues, with over half of the platform's daily volume now on traditional markets. 
Unlike other on-chain trading platforms, Variational aggregates liquidity from both traditional and on-chain markets, making this dual approach integral to its strategy.
“I think there’s a place for both of us in the ecosystem, especially because again, we’re building just a very different type of product for TradFi trading,” said Variational chief executive officer Lucas Schuermann. 
While the platform is often viewed as a Hyperliquid rival, Schuermann said they're setting their sights on brokerages like Robinhood Markets Inc. and Interactive Brokers LLC. 
The company plans to invest the raised capital in strengthening the traditional part of its ecosystem: scaling swap markets, launching a public trading API, and moving swaps toward 24/7 trading. 
The Perpetual Boom Meets a Fractured Regulatory Environment
  Perpetuals are the latest and the hottest trend in the global finance ecosystem. In October, Intercontinental Exchange Inc. invested in Trade [XYZ], which deploys perpetuals for traditional assets on Hyperliquid. 
In November 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in the US allowed perpetual futures on single stocks could begin trading on regulated U.S. exchanges, subject to joint CFTC and SEC oversight. 
In the EU, perpetuals are not explicitly banned for retail traders, but regulators may treat them as derivatives. In the UK, it is strictly forbidden to offer crypto derivatives to retail traders. 
Meanwhile, Variational’s services are not available in the US, Canada and several other prohibited jurisdictions. EU and UK citizens are not excluded, though their access remains subject to local laws and additional platform-level restrictions.


This article was written by Tanya Chepkova at www.financemagnates.com.

Palo Alto Networks Inc (NASDAQ:PANW) posted financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 after the closing bell on Wednesday. Here’s a rundown of the cybersecurity company’s report.

Palo Alto Q1 Earnings Highlights
Palo Alto reported first-quarter revenue of $3.45 billion, beating analyst estimates of $3.31 billion. The company reported adjusted earnings of $1.05 per share for the quarter, beating estimates of 97 cents per share, according to Benzinga Pro.
