title: Bitwise Targets Texas Stock Exchange for New Zcash ETF Under ZEC Ticker
description: Bitwise targets expansion toward regulated investment access to Zcash through a proposed spot exchange-traded fund (ETF) that would list on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE). The move adds another competitor to the growing market for US-listed crypto investment products focused on privacy-oriented digital assets. According to a registration statement filed with the US Securities and […]
fullContent:
Bitwise targets expansion toward regulated investment access to Zcash through a proposed spot exchange-traded fund (ETF) that would list on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE). The move adds another competitor to the growing market for US-listed crypto investment products focused on privacy-oriented digital assets.

According to a registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on November 17, the proposed Bitwise Zcash ETF would trade under the ticker symbol ZEC and hold the cryptocurrency directly.

The filing outlines the fund’s structure and service providers, although the product cannot begin trading until its registration statement becomes effective.

Bitwise Names Texas Stock Exchange as Proposed ETF Venue

The Form S-1 identifies the Texas Stock Exchange as the anticipated listing venue for the fund, marking a change from an earlier draft submitted on October 16 that named NYSE Arca.

The proposed ETF would seek to track the value of its underlying Zcash holdings, after accounting for operating expenses and other liabilities. Its net asset value would be calculated using the CF Zcash-Dollar US Settlement Price, a benchmark provided by CF Benchmarks.

Coinbase Custody would be responsible for safeguarding the fund’s ZEC holdings, while Bitwise Investment Advisers would act as the ETF’s sponsor and manager. The filing also leaves the proposed annual sponsor fee unspecified. As a result, investors do not yet have a confirmed figure for the fund’s management costs.

Importantly, the registration statement has not become effective, meaning the ETF has not started trading and its proposed listing is not yet finalized.

Zcash ETF Competition Expands Across US Exchanges

Bitwise’s filing comes as established asset managers and other financial firms seek to offer regulated exposure to Zcash through traditional investment markets.

Grayscale launched its Zcash ETF on NYSE Arca in August, providing US investors with access to spot ZEC exposure through an exchange-traded product. The fund trades under the ticker ZCSH. Winklevoss Asset Services also entered the competition in October after filing to launch a separate spot Zcash ETF on Nasdaq. Its proposed product would trade under the ticker WINK.

Bitwise’s application would add another option to this developing market, while its choice of the Texas Stock Exchange distinguishes the proposal from products targeting more established US trading venues. The growing number of applications suggests that asset managers are looking beyond Bitcoin and Ether as they explore demand for investment products tied to other digital assets.

What the Proposed Listing Means for Zcash

A spot Zcash ETF could give traditional investors a way to gain exposure to ZEC through brokerage accounts without having to purchase and manage the cryptocurrency directly.

However, the proposed product’s progress will depend on the SEC registration process and the effectiveness of its filing. Until those requirements are met, the fund remains a proposal rather than an available investment option.

For now, Bitwise’s decision to name TXSE as its intended exchange adds another development to the expanding US market for crypto-linked investment products. Competition among issuers could give investors more ways to access digital assets through traditional financial markets, although the final terms and launch timeline remain uncertain.

Could Bitwise’s proposed Zcash ETF increase institutional interest in ZEC? Will the Texas Stock Exchange become a more important venue for crypto investment products?

Grayscale launched its Zcash ETF on NYSE Arca in August, providing US investors with access to spot ZEC exposure through an exchange-traded product. The fund trades under the ticker ZCSH. Winklevoss Asset Services also entered the competition in October after filing to launch a separate spot Zcash ETF on Nasdaq. Its proposed product would trade under the ticker WINK.

Bitwise’s application would add another option to this developing market, while its choice of the Texas Stock Exchange distinguishes the proposal from products targeting more established US trading venues. The growing number of applications suggests that asset managers are looking beyond Bitcoin and Ether as they explore demand for investment products tied to other digital assets.

What the Proposed Listing Means for Zcash

A spot Zcash ETF could give traditional investors a way to gain exposure to ZEC through brokerage accounts without having to purchase and manage the cryptocurrency directly.

However, the proposed product’s progress will depend on the SEC registration process and the effectiveness of its filing. Until those requirements are met, the fund remains a proposal rather than an available investment option.

For now, Bitwise’s decision to name TXSE as its intended exchange adds another development to the expanding US market for crypto-linked investment products. Competition among issuers could give investors more ways to access digital assets through traditional financial markets, although the final terms and launch timeline remain uncertain.

The post Investment Scams Cost Americans $27,500,000 in Eight Months, Topping Online Purchase Fraud appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
Investment scams have cost Americans $27.5 million in reported losses over eight months, more than any other fraud type that commonly targets older adults.

Homewatch CareGivers says it analyzed Better Business Bureau Scam Tracker reports from January 1st to August 24th.

Online purchase fraud was the most reported scam, with 53,934 reports and $25 million in losses.

Phishing was second by volume, with 27,389 reports and $9 million in losses.

Investment scams ranked lower in volume, with 1,110 reports. Even so, their losses were the highest of any category in the study at $27.5 million.

“Although Online Purchase fraud and Phishing are the most commonly reported scams targeting seniors, Investment scams cost Americans more money. The Better Business Bureau tracked 1,110 Investment scams in our data period, and there were 15 types of scams that were more prevalent than this. But because of the high figures involved in investment scams, the total reported loss equals $27.5 million — three times the cost of Phishing to scam victims and dozens of times the cost of most other fraud types.”

Las Vegas had the highest rate of scams that commonly target seniors among 25 major cities, at 97 per 100,000 residents over an eight-month period.

Victims in Houston lost $1,009,000 to investment fraud, representing 9% of the total losses in the fraud category in Texas.

New Hampshire had the highest rate among states, with 816 reports, or 58 per 100,000 residents.

The figures include reports from victims of all ages, not just seniors.

title: Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam
Coinbase said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million, roughly 91% of what customers tried to send, from reaching scammers running a deepfake Elon Musk crypto giveaway.
This post Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam

Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.”

Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers.

A livestream that wasn’t real

The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said.

Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send.

The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves.

“Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said.

How the agent works

Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart.

Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data.

“It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed.

Cheaper fakes

Coinbase said deepfakes have changed the economics of the scam. Staging something like this once took “a crew, a studio, and weeks,” it wrote. “Now it takes a livestream slot and a model.” The company said it is expanding AI review of risky sends to every type of scam, not just high-profile ones, and is also using AI to label new scam cases so its models learn from attacks within hours instead of weeks.

Social engineering has been a steady problem for Coinbase customers. In September, a Brooklyn man was sentenced to 12 years in prison over a $16 million Coinbase phishing scam. This week, Trezor customers reported scam calls after a breach at the hardware wallet maker’s shipping partner exposed 27,000 orders.

The post came the same day Coinbase launched a ChatGPT plugin for trading bitcoin, stocks and derivatives, which requires users to approve every order. Coinbase closed the post with a list of things it will never do, including promising to double, triple or multiply crypto that customers send.

“Nobody legitimate will double your crypto,” the company wrote.

This post Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Analyst Calls BTC's $62,000 Washout the Year's Third 'Fat Pitch' as Bitcoin Slips
description: Bitcoin slid toward $64,000 as an analyst called the drop the year's third fat pitch. RSI flashes oversold, but $59,000 support is the level buyers must hold.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • An unnamed analyst called Bitcoin's slide into the low $60,000s the year's third 'fat pitch' for buyers.
  • Momentum gauges flash deeply oversold, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Buyers face their real test at the last mapped support on the chart.

Bitcoin's sharp November sell-off has drawn a bold call from one analyst. The analyst described the washout as the third 'fat pitch' of the year, meaning a rare chance to buy cheaply.

That view lands while sellers still steer the market and every recent bounce has faded. Bitcoin now sits near a support band that also marks the bottom of the washout zone. Traders want to know if dip buyers will defend it or let it break.

An Analyst Sees a Buying Chance in Bitcoin's Slide

An analyst has called Bitcoin's drop to $62,000 the third "fat pitch" of the year. In baseball, a fat pitch is an easy ball to hit. In markets, it means a strong buying opportunity. The analyst has not been publicly identified, and no further detail on the reasoning has been released.

The slide behind that call runs deep. Bitcoin traded near $64,150 at 6:30 a.m. ET on Nov 18, according to a daily price report. That was down about 1.3% from roughly $65,000 the prior day.

Over a year, the picture looks harsher. The same report showed Bitcoin about 31% below its level a year earlier, when it traded near $92,900. Its market value stood at about $1.33 trillion.

Dip buyers now have a story to rally around, but a story alone does not lift prices. Buyers still need the market to stop falling and show it can hold a floor.

Bitcoin Trades Far Below a $76K Ceiling

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Bitcoin now trades near $64,000, well under its two most-watched trend lines. The 50-day moving average, which tracks the average closing price over roughly the past ten weeks, sits near $76,000. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, has drifted to almost the same spot.

That overlap matters. When both averages sit at one level, they form a single, thick ceiling. Any rebound would likely meet sellers there, since many buyers from recent months would be looking to exit near breakeven.

The recent losses explain the gap. Bitcoin shed about 14% over the past week alone. Over 30 days, the drop stretches to roughly 23%, leaving the coin near the bottom of its monthly range.

A month earlier, Bitcoin changed hands near $81,440. That slide wiped out most of the gains buyers had banked through the early fall.

Trend readings confirm that sellers are steering. The direction gauges show a real, established trend, and it points lower. Momentum also keeps pointing down, with no sign yet that the selling has run its course.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Selling Yet

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, has dropped to about 21. Readings under 30 count as oversold. In plain terms, sellers have pushed so hard and so fast that they may be running short of fuel.

Readings this stretched often come before relief bounces. Traders who sold late tend to buy back, and bargain hunters step in. That pattern gives the analyst's call some support.

The selling has not paused yet, though. Bitcoin slipped another 2% over the past day. Momentum gauges still point lower, so downside pressure has not turned.

Oversold markets can stay oversold for weeks. For the fat pitch to become hittable, momentum needs to flip first. Until then, a low RSI marks exhaustion, and buyers still have to prove they are back.

Where $59K Support Meets the Washout Zone

The nearest floor on the daily chart sits near $59,000. That level lies just under the analyst's washout zone, forming one band where buyers would need to show up.

Below that level, the data maps no support. A daily close beneath it would leave Bitcoin in open air, with no clear level to slow the fall. Sellers who have controlled the trend would gain fresh room to press.

Overhead, the first barrier stands near $75,000. A move back there would put price right against the twin moving averages. That would be the first real test of whether buyers can turn the trend.

Beyond that, resistance waits near $80,000. Clearing it would undo much of the recent damage. For now, both levels look distant from the current price.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

The next few sessions should show which side owns that support band.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce holds the nearest floor and pushes price back toward the first resistance level under the moving averages. A daily close below that floor would cancel this path.
  • Bearish: Sellers break the floor, and with no mapped support beneath it the sell-off extends quickly. A recovery above the first resistance level would invalidate this view and suggest the washout has ended.

Buyers Still Need Proof

Value buyers have a fair case. Bitcoin sits deep in oversold territory, and the analyst's call gives them a reason to watch closely. The trend has not confirmed it, though. Sellers still lead, and momentum has not turned. Patient buyers may want proof before they swing.

title: Nvidia Earnings Surge as Board Rejects Huang’s Return and Bitcoin Eyes $60K
description: Nvidia earnings delivered a fresh boost to market sentiment after the chipmaker reported record quarterly revenue and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook. The results helped lift technology stocks and supported Bitcoin’s recovery, although concerns surrounding the broader crypto market remain. The positive earnings report came alongside a major leadership development: Nvidia’s board rejected calls to reinstate former […]
fullContent:
Nvidia earnings delivered a fresh boost to market sentiment after the chipmaker reported record quarterly revenue and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook. The results helped lift technology stocks and supported Bitcoin’s recovery, although concerns surrounding the broader crypto market remain.

The positive earnings report came alongside a major leadership development: Nvidia’s board rejected calls to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, despite his public willingness to return. Meanwhile, Bitcoin continued trading within a narrow range as investors monitored liquidity around the $60,000 level.

Nvidia Earnings Beat Expectations Despite Leadership Turmoil

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, representing a 103% increase from the same period last year. The figure exceeded analyst expectations of $109.3 billion by approximately 5.6%, highlighting continued demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, accounting for roughly 93% of the company’s total sales.

The chipmaker also provided an optimistic outlook for the current quarter, projecting revenue of approximately $130 billion. That compares with Wall Street expectations of around $125.3 billion, suggesting that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains strong.

However, the financial performance came amid uncertainty surrounding the company’s leadership.

Board chairman Harvey Jones confirmed during the earnings call that directors had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. The announcement followed Huang’s earlier statement that he would be honored to return if the board believed it was in shareholders’ best interests.

Nvidia shares initially closed 0.4% lower at $155.46 on Tuesday before gaining approximately 4% in after-hours trading following the earnings announcement.

Bitcoin Recovers as Nvidia Boosts Market Sentiment

Nvidia’s results provided some relief across financial markets, with Bitcoin recovering into its recent $64,000–$66,000 trading range.

The cryptocurrency had briefly slipped below that range on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia’s earnings announcement, extending concerns following its recent decline toward $62,000, an 18-week low recorded over the weekend.

The improvement in sentiment also extended to traditional markets. Nvidia shares gained approximately 3% in Wednesday premarket trading, while Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 1%. South Korea’s KOSPI Composite also climbed 2%, closing at 5,067 points and recovering above the closely watched 5,000 threshold.

Although the developments suggest renewed confidence in technology-related assets, Bitcoin’s recovery remains relatively limited. Investors are still assessing liquidity conditions, interest-rate expectations and the possibility of further downside across risk markets.

Glassnode Identifies $60K as Critical Bitcoin Liquidity Zone

Despite Bitcoin’s stabilization, market participants continue watching the $60,000 level as an important area for potential support.

According to Glassnode, Binance and Coinbase order-book data show that resting buy orders within 5% of Bitcoin’s current price outweigh sell orders by approximately 2.3 times. The research firm also identified the $60,000 region as the largest individual bid concentration on Binance since August.

This suggests that buyers are positioning themselves around the level, potentially providing a cushion if selling pressure returns.

However, Glassnode warned that a move toward $60,000 could trigger additional liquidations among traders holding leveraged long positions, potentially accelerating a decline. The firm added that most forced position closures had already occurred during the initial sell-off.

For now, Nvidia’s earnings have offered a temporary improvement in market sentiment, but Bitcoin still needs to establish stronger support before a sustained recovery becomes clearer.

Could Nvidia’s strong earnings help Bitcoin regain its bullish momentum, or will broader market uncertainty continue weighing on prices? Will the $60,000 liquidity zone provide enough support to prevent another major sell-off?

fullContent:

fullContent:
Bitcoin (BTC USD) trades near $64,000 on Wednesday, November 18, the day before Anthropic’s shares start trading on Nasdaq, and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes says the listing will set Bitcoin’s direction. If the Anthropic IPO pops, Hayes told the New Era Finance Podcast, “it’s game back on. It’s long everything. Risk on.” He added: “Bitcoin’s going to go up too.”

LATEST: Arthur Hayes says Anthropic’s IPO is “the bellwether for the whole story,” telling the New Era Finance Podcast that if it pops, “it’s game back on. It’s long everything. Risk on.”

“Bitcoin’s going to go up too.” pic.twitter.com/RPzyHUnpu9

— CoinMarketCap (@CoinMarketCap) November 18, 2026

It’s a clean, testable call. So we tested it against the last 12 big IPOs. When a listing jumped 20% or more on its first day, BTC USD was up a median 2% a month later. When it didn’t, Bitcoin was up a median 12%.

Bitcoin needs a lift. It is down 13% in a week, and the Fear & Greed Index, a daily sentiment gauge from 0 to 100, sits at 11, deep in “extreme fear.”

So does an Anthropic pop really mean a Bitcoin rally?

BTC USD After 12 Big IPOs: The Pops Didn’t Pay

We took 12 large listings since 2019, from Uber to SpaceX. For each one, we compared the stock’s first-day close with its IPO price, then measured Bitcoin from the listing day to 7 and 30 days later, using Binance’s daily closes.

  • Big pops: six IPOs jumped 20% or more on day one: Figma, Circle, Airbnb, Snowflake, Rivian and Arm. A week later, Bitcoin was up after four of them, but only by a median 0.9%. A month later, the median was 2%.
  • Small or no pops: after the other six, Bitcoin was up 30 days later five times, with a median gain of 12%. Uber fell 8% on its first day in 2019, and Bitcoin rose 20% over the next month.
  • The closest case: SpaceX gained 19% on its first day in June. BTC USD was flat a week later and flat a month later.

Twelve listings is a small sample, and the market around each one mattered more than the stock. Airbnb’s +120% month came in the December 2020 bull run, and Rivian’s −27% month came at the November 2021 top. What the numbers don’t show is a link between a hot debut and a Bitcoin rally.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Below Its 200-Week Average for the First Time Since 2022: Is a Drop to $50K Coming or a Historic Buying Opportunity?

Hayes Sees Anthropic as a Test of Risk Appetite

Hayes’s point is less about Anthropic than about mood. A strong debut for the largest AI listing would show that investors are willing to buy risk again, and Bitcoin usually trades as a risk asset. On November 11, he wrote on X that he was adding crypto exposure ahead of the listing, while keeping his positions small enough to exit quickly.

Demand for the shares looks strong. Anthropic set a price range of $70 to $78 a share in its roadshow announcement. The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that demand could push the price above $80. On Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange, a pre-IPO contract on the shares trades about 24% above that.

The other side is money. At the top of the range, the listing raises about $64 billion. Some of that cash comes from investors selling other assets, and Bitcoin slid about 20% in the weeks before SpaceX’s record listing in June.

DISCOVER: Top 20 Crypto to Buy in 2026

BTC USD Price Analysis: $65,500 Is the First Test

On the daily chart, BTC USD trades at $64,069. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,755, and its 200-day EMA at $75,753.

  • Resistance: $65,500, a level Bitcoin bounced from in February, March and April and was turned back from in June, July and August. Above that, $74,300, which capped prices in March and held as a floor in April, May and September.
  • Support: $62,300, Sunday’s low. Bitcoin bounced near it in February, June, July and August. Below it, $57,800, the July low and the bottom of the past year.
Path What has to happen Next stop
Bullish A strong Anthropic debut and a daily close above $65,500 $74,300, the March-September level
Sideways A modest debut, price between $62,300 and $65,500 A range near current levels
Bearish A weak debut or a daily close below $62,300 $57,800, the July low

Hayes may still be right about the mood. But if history is a guide, a big Anthropic pop is not enough on its own. BTC USD needs buyers to come back to crypto, not just to AI stocks.

title: Decentralized Lottery Protocol CoinLotto Completes The Smart Contract Security Audit with CertiK and Launches on Mainnet
description: Decentralized lottery protocol CoinLotto has announced the completion of an independent smart-contract security audit by blockchain security firm CertiK.
fullContent:
Decentralized lottery protocol CoinLotto has completed a smart-contract security audit with CertiK and launched on mainnet.

Decentralized lottery protocol CoinLotto has announced the completion of an independent smart-contract security audit by blockchain security firm CertiK. 

The audit evaluated CoinLotto’s smart contracts, which handle ticket sales, prize pool accumulation, winner selection, and distribution across multiple blockchain networks. By pairing CertiK’s external security evaluation with public on-chain execution and cryptographically verifiable randomness, CoinLotto aims to establish a fully transparent foundation for decentralized lotteries.

Verifiable Fairness and Immutable Prize Pools

Traditional online lottery systems often rely on off-chain execution or centralized servers for prize draws. In contrast, CoinLotto runs its core lottery logic directly on-chain. Ticket purchases, prize pools, draw schedules, winner selection, and payouts are all recorded publicly, ensuring that any participant can verify the protocol’s operations.

To guarantee unbiased outcomes, CoinLotto integrates Chainlink VRF 2.5 to supply cryptographically verifiable randomness for every draw. Winners are drawn directly from active, purchased tickets rather than requiring players to match arbitrary number sequences. 

A central feature of the architecture is its immutable prize pool management:

  • Tamper-proof escrow: all entry funds are held in immutable smart contracts that prevent organizers or protocol owners from arbitrarily withdrawing or redirecting assets.

  • Fixed rules: each lottery's parameters are set permanently at creation.

  • Complete winner allocations: upon draw finalization, 100% of the calculated final prize pool is allocated to winning tickets under predefined rules without manual operator intervention.

Permissionless Infrastructure for Community Lotteries

Beyond operating its native protocol lotteries, CoinLotto functions as a permissionless platform where projects, creators, and Web3 communities can launch custom lotteries.

Organizers can configure the following parameters using CoinLotto’s underlying on-chain infrastructure: 

  • Flexible parameters: creators set the entry token, ticket price, ticket limit, draw date, and distribution model.

  • Custom fees: organizers can retain a Creator Fee of up to 30%.

  • Prize models: support for three distinct payout structures – tier (predefined winning positions), win rate (target percentage of winning tickets), and multiplier (target payout relative to ticket cost).

  • Sponsorship top-ups: external wallets can deposit extra funds into active prize pools without triggering Protocol or Creator fees, allowing sponsors to boost rewards directly.

Ecosystem Mechanics and Multi-Chain Support

The protocol introduces three interconnected types of lotteries:

  1. Protocol lotteries: maintained directly by CoinLotto. Every ticket issued, whether winning or non-winning, earns players $CLT tokens.

  2. Super lotteries: high-tier events players can only enter using $CLT tokens. These events are funded by 10% of ticket revenue from linked protocol lotteries as well as direct top-ups.

  3. User-created lotteries: custom lotteries deployed by users utilizing their preferred tokens.

CoinLotto features permanent, on-chain referral tracking. Once registered, referral relationships cannot be overwritten or changed. Referrers automatically earn 50% of Protocol Fees generated by their invites, 10 $CLT upon an invitee's first Protocol ticket purchase, and a 5% bonus on all $CLT earned by referred players.

To broaden access, CoinLotto supports BNB Chain, Base, and Ethereum, allowing projects across major EVM-compatible ecosystems to leverage its infrastructure. Additionally, all claimable funds, referral commissions, and earned $CLT tokens carry no expiration dates, allowing users to claim their funds at any time directly through on-chain transactions.

About CoinLotto

CoinLotto is a multi-chain decentralized lottery protocol designed to bring complete transparency, verifiable randomness, and permissionless gaming infrastructure to Web3. Built on immutable smart contracts and powered by Chainlink VRF 2.5, CoinLotto enables players, creators, and communities to participate in and launch custom lotteries across BNB Chain, Base, and Ethereum. For more information, visit the official documentation at docs.coinlotto.xyz.

Media Contact: cmo@coin-lotto.xyz

Website: https://go.coinlotto.xyz/4iaOOh9 

About CertiK

CertiK was founded in 2017 on the belief that security and compliance must be built into digital asset systems from the very beginning. That is why CertiK brings together formal verification, security auditing, continuous monitoring, risk intelligence, and compliance capabilities within a unified risk management framework. Our goal is not simply to identify vulnerabilities. It is to reduce risk exposure across the digital asset lifecycle, moving organizations from reactive patching toward proactive and continuous risk management.

title: Solana Price Chart After CoinShares Sells SOL: The $67 Support Is the Line to Watch
description: CoinShares sold half its Solana treasury to fund a buyback. SOL trades below both moving averages, and $67 support is the only mapped floor. See the key levels.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • CoinShares sold half its Solana treasury in October to help fund a stock buyback.
  • SOL trades below both key moving averages, and sellers still drive the trend despite an oversold reading.
  • One support level is the only mapped floor, and nothing sits beneath it on the chart.

CoinShares has cut its Solana holdings in half and sold all of its corporate Ether to buy back its own shares.

The sale is small, but it lands on a fragile SOL chart after weeks of heavy losses. Traders want to know if buyers can defend the nearest floor before others follow.

CoinShares Trades Half Its Solana for Its Own Stock

The Jersey-based digital asset manager announced a share buyback of up to $40 million on Oct 27.

The Ether sale raised about $16.6 million, the company said. The Solana sale added roughly $2.7 million. Together the two sales brought in $19.3 million, a little under half the buyback ceiling.

Shareholders approved buybacks on Sept 15, covering up to 25% of outstanding shares. That authority runs until the next annual meeting, expected in the second quarter of 2027. The board said repurchasing stock is a better use of capital than holding digital assets on the balance sheet.

The company sold from a position of strength. Assets under management reached $7.4 billion in the third quarter, up 34.5% from the end of June. Net inflows came in near $125 million.

Quarterly net profit rose to $39.6 million from $31.2 million a year earlier. CSHR shares jumped 5.3% in pre-market trading after the news, against a 52-week high of $10.43.

Both Moving Averages Now Sit Overhead

Solana (SOL) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Solana traded near $74 on Wednesday, well below both of the averages traders watch most. The 50-day moving average, the mean closing price over the past 50 sessions, sits near $93. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, is higher still at about $96.

That stacking matters for anyone holding SOL. Price under both lines means recent buyers and long-term holders alike are sitting on losses. Both averages now act as ceilings, and rallies toward them tend to meet sellers looking to exit near breakeven.

The 50-day line also sits below the 200-day line. That order signals the short-term trend has weakened faster than the long-term one. Charts with that shape usually need weeks of base building before a lasting recovery.

SOL has fallen about 29% in a month. The past week alone cut roughly 11% from the price.

Trading in the last 24 hours was calmer, with a dip of about 1%. That small move suggests selling has slowed for now. It does not show buyers taking control.

A drop of this size has bigger causes than the CoinShares sale. A few million dollars of SOL is a rounding error against the token's daily trading volume. The sale still fits the broader mood, though.

Sellers Stay in Charge Despite an Oversold Reading

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads about 29. Anything below 30 counts as oversold. That means sellers have pushed the price down unusually fast in recent weeks.

Oversold readings often bring a short relief bounce. A bounce of that kind can fade within days, though. Oversold describes the speed of a drop and says nothing about when it ends.

Other gauges still point lower. MACD, a tool that compares short and longer price trends, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downside momentum has not yet turned. Trend strength readings also show a real trend in place, and sellers are the ones driving it. For now, any rebound looks like a pause inside a downtrend.

The Floor With Nothing Mapped Below

Support sits near $67, roughly 9% under the current price. The data shows no further support level below it. If that floor gives way, the chart offers little guidance on where buyers might return.

A close under that floor would leave SOL in open air. Price could slide quickly toward the low $60s before any real demand shows up. Traders often place stop orders just below a clear floor, and a break can trigger them all at once.

Resistance stands near $98, close to where both moving averages cluster. That zone holds the most sellers waiting to exit. A clean move above it would put price back over both averages and flip the structure in favor of buyers.

The next ceiling after that sits around $104. For now, both levels look far away.

What Flips the Next Three Days

Two outcomes look most likely over the next three sessions, and the support floor decides between them.

  • Bullish: The oversold reading sparks a relief bounce that holds above support and carries SOL toward the 50-day average. Buyers would need to stay in control for several sessions. A close below the floor would cancel this case.
  • Bearish: A daily close under support extends the slide into territory with no mapped floor. A recovery back above the 50-day average would invalidate this view and point to a deeper rebound.

Oversold but Not Yet Bottomed

Buyers need to reclaim both moving averages before the trend can turn. Until then, the support floor is the level to defend.

The bigger risk is copycat selling. If more corporate treasuries choose cash over tokens, fresh supply could hit a floor with nothing mapped beneath it.

fullContent:
Oracle released its November edition of Critical Security Patch Update. The update received patches for 655 security vulnerabilities. Some of the vulnerabilities addressed in this update impact more than one product. These patches address vulnerabilities in various product families, including third-party components in Oracle products.

Out of the 655 security updates published, a total of 62 (9.5%) vulnerabilities are rated critical, 249 are rated as important (38%), and 274 are rated as medium.

In this Oracle Critical Security Patch Update, Oracle Hyperion received the highest number of patches, 267, constituting about 41% of the total patches released.

71 of the 655 (about 11%) security patches provided by the November Critical Security Patch Update are for non-Oracle CVEs, such as open-source components included in and exploitable within Oracle product distributions.

This batch of security patches received 20 updates for Oracle Database products. The following is the product-wise distribution: 

  • 7 new security updates for Oracle Database Server with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.9.
    • None of these updates applies to client-only deployments of the Oracle Database.
  • 2 new security updates for Oracle APEX with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.8.
  • 3 new security updates for Oracle Autonomous Health Framework with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.1.
  • 8 new security updates for Oracle REST Data Services with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.8.

The complete list of Oracle product families and the no of patches issued are listed below:

Notable Oracle Vulnerabilities Patched

Oracle Hyperion

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Hyperion received 267 security patches. Out of these, 107 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

A total of 12 vulnerabilities have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Supply Chain

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Supply Chain received 74 security patches. Out of these, 36 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114980, CVE-2026-127324, CVE-2026-127325, CVE-2026-127326, CVE-2026-127327, and CVE-2026-101356 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle E-Business Suite

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle E-Business Suite received 71 security patches. Out of these, 19 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114880, CVE-2026-114924, CVE-2026-114925, CVE-2026-114863, CVE-2026-101691, and CVE-2026-114881 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Fusion Middleware

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Fusion Middleware received 71 security patches. Out of these, 19 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114880, CVE-2026-114924, CVE-2026-114925, CVE-2026-114863, CVE-2026-101691, and CVE-2026-114881 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Communications

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Communications received 31 security patches. Out of these, 21 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-1229, CVE-2026-41889, and CVE-2026-114820 have critical severity ratings.

title: NEAR Price Squeezed Into a 29-Cent Range by Three Levels
description:
Summary Price sits just above the 0.618 retracement. The 100-day SMA near $3.52 caps rebounds. Candles are testing the channel’s […]
The post NEAR Price Squeezed Into a 29-Cent Range by Three Levels appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Price sits just above the 0.618 retracement.
  • The 100-day SMA near $3.52 caps rebounds.
  • Candles are testing the channel’s upper edge.
  • Moving-average order still favors the longer trend.

On the daily NEAR/USDT chart from Binance, the token trades at $3.34, down 1.59% on the day after opening at $3.40 and moving between $3.31 and $3.43.

Where the reference points come from

Every level that matters here traces back to one move. NEAR bottomed near $1.52 in August and ran to a high close to $5.99 by mid-October, nearly quadrupling in about two months.

Stretch a Fibonacci grid over that rally and the map fills in. The 0.236 sits near $4.93, the 0.382 around $4.28 and the 0.5 near $3.76. Lower down, the 0.618 lands close to $3.23, with the 0.786 around $2.48.

The top took weeks to form. Through late September and most of October, NEAR chopped between the 0.382 area and levels above the 0.236, tagging its high near $6 along the way. It was a grind, not a spike and a crash.

A channel of lower highs

Then the selling got organized and from late October, price slid inside a descending parallel channel, with each bounce peaking below the last one and each low undercutting the one before it.

Volume never screamed panic. The decline inside the channel came without a capitulation-sized spike, and today’s 9.37 million NEAR is moderate. This was steady selling, not a forced flush.

Mid-November brought the real stress test. NEAR slipped below the 0.618, then climbed back over it within days. Traders watch that line closely. It’s the deepest standard retracement that still reads as a pullback inside a bigger advance, and past it only the 0.786 stands between price and losing most of the rally.

Three levels inside 29 cents

The bounce off the 0.618 ran straight into the channel’s upper boundary. The last two sessions sit on that line or just above it. Today’s small red candle shows sellers defending it.

Just overhead waits the 100-day SMA at $3.52, the first ceiling for any rebound. So the squeeze is tight. The 0.618 sits underneath, the 100 SMA above, and the channel line cuts right through the current candles, all within a $0.29 range.

One session poking over a trendline isn’t a breakout. A run of daily closes clearly outside the channel would be. Closes above the 100 SMA would make that case far harder to argue with.

READ MORE:

Why a 5% Stablecoin Return Can Still Cost Holders Money

Bent trend, not a broken one

The 50-day SMA carries the bearish half of the story. At about $4.42, it has rolled over and now slopes down, well above price. That’s the plainest evidence that the medium-term trend has turned against buyers.

Further down, the picture changes. The 200-day SMA at $2.72 is still rising. And the averages haven’t crossed: the 50 still sits above the 100, which still sits above the 200. A bearish crossover would mean a shorter average dropping under a longer one, and none has happened yet. The structure built during the rally is dented, not dismantled.

Momentum backs that read. The 14-day RSI prints 39.65, under the 50 midline, so sellers keep the edge for now. Yet it has hooked higher and sits above its own moving average at 37.02. Through the whole decline, it stayed above the oversold line at 30.

Beyond each edge of the band

Either side can give way first. Here’s what the chart has waiting.

Break above $3.52

A daily close over the 100 SMA, with price outside the channel, brings the 0.5 near $3.76 into view. Past that, the 0.382 around $4.28 and the falling 50 SMA at $4.42 stack into a thicker resistance zone.

Slip below $3.23

If sellers reject the channel top and price loses the 0.618 near $3.23, the rising 200 SMA at $2.72 is the first level in the way. The 0.786 around $2.48 sits beneath it.

What decides the label: neither path is a forecast. As long as NEAR holds the 0.618 and the 200 SMA keeps climbing, the drop from $5.99 still reads as a deep correction of the $1.52 rally. A sustained move below both would turn it into a broken trend.

The first signal won’t be dramatic. It’s a run of daily closes clearly above the channel line, not one candle. If those closes arrive with the RSI back over 50, buyers would hold the momentum edge as well as the structure. Until then, the channel still sets the terms.

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—Claiming that such monitoring efforts had been a waste of government resources, Federal Bureau of Investigation officials announced Friday that the agency would discontinue its longstanding practice of tracking serial killers.

Though the FBI’s Violent Criminal Apprehension Program has historically enjoyed bipartisan approval for its role in the capture of murderers like the Golden State Killer and Samuel Little, the bureau has come under scrutiny in recent months amid the Trump administration’s ongoing efforts to downsize federal agencies. Director Kash Patel has repeatedly argued that Americans should stop expecting the government to hunt down every serial killer who binds and gags victims before tossing their bodies in the trunk of a car. 

“Today we are ending the senseless and inefficient tracking of America’s homicidal maniacs,” said Patel, who stated that the decision to no longer collect information related to serial killers was driven primarily by the high costs associated with processing DNA evidence, identifying human remains, and prosecuting federal murder charges. “The fact is, if a crazed necrophile is chasing you through the woods with a pair of hedge shears, it’s not the taxpayers’ job to bail you out. Those kinds of handouts might have flown with the socialist Biden FBI, but not anymore.”

“Our common-sense position is that these depraved, gratification-seeking murderers aren’t the government’s problem,” Patel added.

Despite Patel’s dismissive attitude toward murders and bloody, violent crime scenes, some experts have voiced concerns that ending federal investigations of active killers such as the San Diego Strangler and the Alabama Ripper could allow rates of serial homicides to rebound to levels not seen since the 1970s. According to reports, the FBI has ceased to archive dozens of human fingers mailed to them by uncaptured serial killers and has sold off its forensics laboratory at Quantico to a Trump-linked condominium developer. Critics argue this move could leave the bureau without the institutional capacity to hunt down any violent psychopaths obsessed with constructing a suit out of human skin who may arise in the future.

Despite these criticisms, a number of Americans expressed concerns about government overreach infringing on the civil liberties of anyone who kills for their own personal pleasure and gratification. 

“I don’t know why these woke liberals are so afraid of serial killers,” said Idaho resident Mike Howe, who noted that there were millions of acres of forest where the decapitated remains of victims were buried and claimed that it was “none of our business.” “There’s things we can do without spending millions of dollars to track down every single mentally unstable auto mechanic targeting brunette women who resemble his domineering mother.”

While the decision to curtail federal investigation of serial killers so far appears to have garnered widespread disapproval from law enforcement agencies and public safety groups, the policy shift nevertheless has its staunch defenders.

 “I get why some people are opposed to this change, but I’m glad the Trump administration is letting me collect more slaves to serve me in the afterlife,” said the Ouroboros Killer, an as-of-yet unidentified murderer who has repeatedly voiced his support for the FBI’s actions in numerous cryptographic ciphers mailed to news-
papers across the country. “It feels so good when I slide that knife in, but even better is when the president takes a knife to wasteful government spending.”

 “Government efficiency is the ultimate thrill,” the Ouroboros continued. “I am not afraid of death because I know that in paradise all the tax dollars Trump has saved by slashing government bloat will be waiting for me. Ouroboros = 31, inefficient federal bureaucracy = 0.”

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—Saying he had only narrowly escaped the encounter with his righteousness intact, House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters Friday he had been the target of a temptation attempt. “Early yesterday afternoon, an unknown assailant put several extremely provocative female mannequins in storefronts along my jogging route in what appears to have been a highly sophisticated plot to corrupt the purity of my everlasting soul,” Johnson said during a press conference at which he addressed the brush with prurience, confirming he had been assessed by a team of top pastors to ensure he had suffered no lasting wickedness from the incident. “Thanks to my security team’s quick-thinking recitation of Bible verses, I was able to remain virtuous long enough to make it home for a cold shower, but the horrible truth is that I could have been aroused that day. These extremists came within a hair’s breadth of titillating a sitting politician, and if those yoga pants had ridden just a little lower on the mannequins’ hips, they might have been successful.” Johnson added that the close call had spurred him to draft a bill that would place a federal ban on the sale of mannequins with defined nipples. 

The post Mike Johnson Claims He Was Target Of Temptation Attempt appeared first on The Onion.

title: The Chopping Block: Crypto's Brutal Week With FalconX's Josh Lim, CZ vs. Star, the Anthropic IPO, and Should Jensen Huang Come Back?
description:
Welcome to The Chopping Block, where crypto insiders Haseeb Qureshi, Tom Schmidt, Tarun Chitra, and Robert Leshner chop it up about the latest in crypto. This week they are joined by Joshua Lim, Global Co-Head of Markets at FalconX.

Six red weeks in a row, BTC down to 65K, the fear and greed index at 10, and a $20 billion contraction in stablecoins. Josh walks through what his desk saw: a hidden buildup in leverage, end-of-year hedges in IBIT puts, and a weekend sell-off concentrated on Coinbase. The hosts react to the Situational Awareness 13F coming out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI. Josh says the numbers don't support Star's claim that Binance is dumping on the market, and Haseeb explains how far back the CZ and Star feud goes. Then the Anthropic IPO: Tarun asks whether a flop would actually be better for crypto, Haseeb bets newly liquid Anthropic employees buy crypto, and Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules are bringing the weirdness back. Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is, and Haseeb and Tarun argue over whether past bear markets ever had a narrative. They close on Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line, Tarun makes the case that he willed NVIDIA into existence, and Haseeb says tech is misreading the moment.

title: Etherscan Hacked? Crypto Users Have Had Enough as Support Security Scare Sparks Alarm
description:
Etherscan hacked? Freshworks, Optimizely, and major banking security incidents raise questions about crypto and traditional finance security.
The post Etherscan Hacked? Crypto Users Have Had Enough as Support Security Scare Sparks Alarm appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Another day, another security scare. This time, Etherscan is warning users after detecting unauthorized access attempts against its customer support system that might have been hacked. But the timing could hardly be worse for an industry already dealing with a growing list of cyberattacks.

The warning comes just days after hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely, injecting malicious code into websites operated by 178 organizations. The affected names included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, and CNN.

Meanwhile, crypto platforms have faced separate attacks involving compromised API keys, protocol vulnerabilities, and stolen customer information. Traditional banking has not escaped either, with a French bank recently losing approximately €100 million to hackers.

So what kind of security era are we entering? The problem is no longer confined to crypto exchanges or experimental DeFi protocols. Banks, technology companies, payment providers and blockchain businesses are increasingly exposed to the same interconnected digital infrastructure.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Etherscan, Optimizely and 178 Websites Hacked: Nobody Seems Safe

Etherscan disclosed just a few minutes ago that attackers had attempted to gain unauthorized access to its Freshworks customer support and ticketing system. The company is investigating and has introduced precautionary measures. It has not confirmed that customer records were successfully accessed, but warned users about suspicious support communications, unexpected links, and requests for sensitive information.

The concern is particularly relevant because support impersonation remains an effective way to steal crypto and your money. An attacker posing as an Etherscan representative could exploit a user’s existing support request to make a phishing message appear legitimate.

But Etherscan is hardly the only name facing security questions this week. Just two days ago, hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation signup process. They injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects, allowing the code to run on websites using the affected software.

Security researchers identified 178 organizations whose websites carried the malicious code. The list included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, Zoom, Salesforce, CNN and Equifax. The injected script attempted to replace crypto wallet addresses with attacker-controlled alternatives. It also targeted payment-card information, cookies and screenshots, while attempting to deliver exploit code against older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed the vulnerability and said it had removed the injected code and fixed the flaw. Its November 17 incident report said the unauthorized party exploited the signup process rather than stealing customer administrator passwords.

The financial damage remains unclear. It is reported that investigators could not establish how many visitors were affected or whether the attempted thefts succeeded.

The uncomfortable takeaway is that attackers did not need to breach 178 separate companies. They exploited one software provider whose code was embedded across hundreds of websites.

Crypto Exchanges and Banks Are Both Taking Hits

Crypto’s security problems extend beyond Etherscan and the Optimizely incident. DeFiLlama’s hack tracker recorded several attacks during the week, including a $10.39 million incident involving Lighter Perps on November 16. The attacker exploited a compromised trader API key, enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

Lighter said its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised. It temporarily suspended withdrawals and activated Guardian mode to prevent further unauthorized activity.

Another incident hit MORE Markets, where an attacker exploited a lending mechanism to drain approximately $308,000 in WFLOW. B18 TimeBank also suffered an exploit on November 17, losing $404,540 in USDC through its reward voucher redemption mechanism.

These incidents show different weaknesses across crypto infrastructure. Not every loss comes from a broken smart contract. Compromised credentials, vulnerable applications and flawed authorization mechanisms can be equally damaging.

Traditional finance faces its own problems. French lender Crédit Mutuel Arkéa disclosed a cyber heist earlier in November, with hackers stealing approximately €100 million through fraudulent transactions originating from the bank’s own accounts. The bank said customer assets were not affected, although some transactions were temporarily suspended.

Deutsche Bank also made headlines on November 17 after confidential internal documents surfaced through an international journalistic investigation. It was a document leak, not a confirmed breach of its current banking systems.

Deutsche Bank said security testing found no indication that its current IT environment, account information, login credentials, or payment data had been compromised. Yet, it has greater effects to geopolitics.

Banking institutions are not immune to major security incidents simply because they operate under traditional financial regulations.

Is Crypto Actually Less Safe Than Traditional Banking?

Crypto has suffered enormous losses. The October Binance incident alone involved $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, making it one of the largest cryptocurrency heists on record. Yet, traditional finance also faces attacks involving payment infrastructure, third-party service providers, and internal transaction systems.

The Optimizely incident is particularly revealing. Both HSBC and Ledger appeared among the affected organizations. The vulnerability did not care whether visitors were interacting with a traditional financial institution or a crypto company.

Neither system offers complete protection. The real question is whether companies can secure the increasingly complex infrastructure connecting their services. A single compromised vendor can expose hundreds of organizations, while one stolen credential can bypass otherwise sophisticated security systems.

Crypto users have every reason to demand stronger protections. But traditional banking customers should not mistake regulation and familiar branding for immunity.

With Etherscan possibly being hacked, the data provider is now joining the growing list of companies investigating security incidents.

title: Cognizant and Qualys Redefine AI-Era Managed Security Service
description: Cognizant will use the full Qualys portfolio to bring its clients what the frontier AI era demands: AI-speed detection, hyper-prioritization, and confident remediation for every zero-day. When a critical zero-day goes public, security leaders ask two questions: which assets are affected, and how fast can we safely fix them? For most enterprises, the current answer […]
fullContent:
Cognizant will use the full Qualys portfolio to bring its clients what the frontier AI era demands: AI-speed detection, hyper-prioritization, and confident remediation for every zero-day.

When a critical zero-day goes public, security leaders ask two questions: which assets are affected, and how fast can we safely fix them? For most enterprises, the current answer is days, then weeks.

Frontier AI makes that remediation timeframe dangerous. Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday alone carried 1,093 vulnerabilities, up from 93 in November 2025 before frontier AI models arrived. AI-assisted attackers can weaponize a new advisory in four to twelve hours, while scan-driven detection often takes 24 to 36 hours just to show which assets are affected. The risk is already real: Cognizant’s 2026 Cybersecurity Pulse Poll found that 83% of participating U.S. enterprises had an AI-related security incident in the past 24 months.

Knowing what to fix is only half the gap. Every step from finding to fix is still gated by people, for one reason: fear that a patch will break production, that a reboot will take down a critical system, or that there is no fast way back. Teams will not hand fixes to automation they do not trust.

Cognizant helps the world’s largest enterprises scale with AI, through its AI Builder approach, and recognizes that its clients need security that moves at machine speed. Already running managed services on Qualys ETM, Cognizant is now expanding to the full Qualys portfolio, including TruRisk Eliminate. That is why I am excited to welcome Cognizant to the Qualys Global mROC Alliance.

Managed detection is table stakes. This is the dawn of the 24-hour autonomous remediation service, run from Qualys ETM: a zero-day disclosed, detected, prioritized, and remediated within a day.

Why the Qualys Platform Fits Cognizant’s Approach

Running zero-day response as a service, at enterprise scale, puts specific demands on the platform underneath. Cognizant needed three capabilities working as one:

  • One record for every asset, across every tool, built from Qualys and non-Qualys sources, so there is no reconciling data across disparate tools before anyone can act.
  • Exploit validation in each client’s own environment, so every hour of the client’s team’s time goes to risk that is real.
  • Remediation with confidence, so automation can be trusted within production systems.

Qualys delivers all three on one platform, with the agentic AI to run them at machine speed.

Cognizant brings what a platform alone cannot: Cyber Vulnerability Management services and threat intelligence, delivery experience inside large enterprises, and a view of risk in financial terms for the board. Its operators run the Risk Operations Center, powered by Qualys ETM to navigate inside each client’s own tools, change windows, and approvals. Clients keep control of what gets fixed and when. Cognizant carries the daily work.

“Our 2026 Cybersecurity Pulse Poll shows that strength in one control, such as detection or remediation, still leaves enterprises exposed in the AI era. Together with Qualys, we are connecting detection, prioritization and remediation into one managed operating model, helping clients reduce risk, strengthen resilience and scale AI with confidence.”
— Vishal Salvi, SVP and Global Head of Cybersecurity, Cognizant

Cognizant will deliver four mROC services on the Qualys platform:

  • Cyber risk quantification and advisory services. Cyber risk for business applications shown in dollars, with a personalized risk plan and a report for the board.
  • Onboarding and integration. The security tools a customer already owns connected into one record for each asset, with data quality checked from day one.
  • Risk monitoring as a managed service. AI-speed alerts on new CVEs, a validated queue instead of noise, and a weekly exposure review, using InstaScan, Agent Val, and ROCky.

Risk remediation as a managed service. A wave-based plan built from the Risk Elimination Playbook, zero-touch remediation where it is safe, and proof the fix held, using TruRisk Eliminate, TruConfidence, and Agent Sara.

AI-Speed Detection: Every Exposure Known in Minutes

Frontier AI has changed the rhythm of disclosure. Vulnerabilities now land in volume, and attackers act on them in hours, well inside any scan cycle.

Qualys InstaScan, delivered by Agent Insta, closes that gap. It turns the inventory and telemetry a client already has, from Qualys and non-Qualys sources, into high-confidence findings within minutes of disclosure. No new scan, no new agent.

On November’s Patch Tuesday, InstaScan delivered 90% of detections within minutes. The first landed about 40 minutes before Microsoft’s own release notes went live. With Cognizant, that speed turns into action. Through its risk monitoring service, Cognizant analysts watch for new disclosures every day, confirm each exposure, and route it to the right asset owner with context. The client’s team no longer chases owners or rebuilds asset lists every time a new CVE trends.

Hyper-Prioritization: Proven Exploitability

More vulnerabilities do not mean more risk. Of the 48,172 vulnerabilities disclosed in 2025, the Qualys Threat Research Unit found only 357 (0.74%) confirmed remotely exploitable and actively weaponized. No team can work the full list, and none should have to.

Agent Val and TruConfirm test what is actually exploitable in the client’s own environment, with existing controls counted. Critical on paper but blocked by a control? It leaves the urgent queue. Exploitable on a PCI-scoped server? It goes to the top.

Cyber Risk Quantification (CRQ) then puts validated risk in dollars, by business application, so the CISO can show the board what each fix is worth.

With Cognizant, the short list becomes a working rhythm. Through its risk monitoring and advisory services, Cognizant keeps each client’s validated queue current and reviews it with them every week. The client’s team stops triaging noise and starts each week knowing exactly what to fix first.

Autonomous Remediation: Remediate with Confidence and Maintain Operational Resiliency

That fear is why the global mean time to remediate sits at about 30 days. TruRisk Eliminate, with TruConfidence, removes it by protecting operational resiliency before, during, and after every change.

  • Before: TruRisk Eliminate chooses the safest fix for each finding: patch, mitigate, isolate, or uninstall. A patch reliability score decides what deploys automatically and what goes ring by ring.
  • During: Changes roll out in waves, starting with low-risk rings. System health is watched through each wave, and rollback restores a known-good state if health drops.
  • After: AI-powered patch failure analysis pinpoints why a change failed and the corrective actions, and automated rollback restores a known-good state.

Showing clients the 1% that matters

Cognizant can open every client engagement with a Risk Elimination Playbook, powered by TruConfidence and built for that client’s environment. It narrows the backlog to the 1% that must be fixed now and moves the rest into planned software updates. It also benchmarks the client’s mean time to remediate against peers, and shows how much of the backlog autonomous remediation can close, and how much faster.

It becomes the plan behind every remediation wave and the baseline for every review.

Where Managed Security Goes Next

The three pillars together provide a new kind of service: 24-hour autonomous remediation, run from ETM. Cognizant can take a critical zero-day from disclosure to remediation within a day, for every client, with operational resiliency built in at every step.

Managed security is moving from raising alerts to closing risk. Cognizant is among the first to deliver that at enterprise scale, and I expect it to set the bar enterprises hold every provider to. That is what the Global mROC Alliance was built for: the platform, the certification path, and the operating model to run the Risk Operations Center as a service.

Attackers already move at AI speed. This expanded partnership helps tip the balance back toward the defense.

To learn more, visit the Qualys Global mROC Alliance page, read the press release, or contact your Cognizant or Qualys account team.

title: Arbitrum Price Drops 19% in Seven Days Despite $7.4M Revenue and USDG Growth
description: Arbitrum booked $7.4 million in revenue and USDG lending passed $153 million, yet ARB fell 19% in a week. Buyers now need to defend support near $0.11.
fullContent:
Arbitrum's latest revenue report shows a network earning steady income from several sources, with stablecoin demand climbing alongside it.

ARB holders have little to show for it. The token kept sliding with a weak crypto market this week. Traders now want to know whether stronger fundamentals can ever lift a token that earns no direct share of fees.

Arbitrum Books $7.4M as USDG Lending Passes $153M

Arbitrum reported $7.4 million in recent revenue in a post on the network's official X account. The haul lifts its 2026 total above $13.6 million. For a layer 2 network that sells faster and cheaper Ethereum transactions, that is a meaningful income line.

The money comes from five separate streams. Transaction fees make up one source, and treasury management makes up another. Spreading income across several channels means the network leans less on any single business.

Stablecoin activity is also growing. Adoption of USDG, a dollar-pegged token, keeps rising on Arbitrum. Lending of USDG on Morpho, a decentralized lending protocol, now holds more than $153 million in total value locked. That figure measures the deposits users have committed to the market, and it signals growing trust in the asset.

Arbitrum has also built ties with traditional finance. The network counts Cross River Bank and SBI Digital Markets as partners. Both firms give the ecosystem a bridge to regulated banking and capital markets, which could draw more institutional users over time.

A Broad Crypto Selloff Swallows the Good News

Those revenue numbers arrived at an awkward moment. Crypto markets are in a broad retreat, and bitcoin is leading the way down. Bitcoin has dropped about 13% over the past week, dragging most major tokens with it.

ARB has fared worse. The token fell roughly 19% over the same seven days. That gap is common for layer 2 tokens, which tend to swing harder than bitcoin in both directions. When traders cut risk, smaller and more speculative assets usually get sold first.

The network's design also limits the boost from good news. Arbitrum's income flows to its DAO treasury, the pool of funds governed by token holders. ARB holders receive no direct share of those fees.

Treasury Gains While Token Holders Wait

The split between network income and token price creates clear winners and losers.

  • DAO and treasury: Steady revenue pays for operations and funds grants without forcing large token sales.
  • ARB holders: The token has lost about 31% over the past month. For now, those price losses outweigh any comfort from stronger fundamentals.
  • USDG issuers and Morpho lenders: Rising stablecoin demand brings more deposits, more borrowing and more fee income.
  • Rival layer 2 networks: Competitors face pressure to show income of their own, or risk looking weaker to builders and investors.

$0.11 Becomes the Floor Bulls Cannot Lose

Arbitrum (ARB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ARB trades near $0.13, down about 3% in the past day. The token sits below its 50-day average near $0.16. It also trades under its 200-day average. Both lines now act as ceilings, which keeps the broader trend in sellers' favor.

Momentum is weak as well. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads 35. That is weak but short of oversold, so there is still room for further selling before buyers typically step in. The MACD indicator also points down.

On the daily chart, the green line marks support near $0.11. Holding that level is the main job for buyers. A clean break would expose the next support around $0.083, a much deeper drop.

Any rebound faces the red line near $0.15. That level matches the 200-day average, which makes it a tough barrier to clear.

What Could Turn ARB Around Next

Three things could shift the picture for ARB in the coming weeks.

  • Revenue and USDG growth: Another strong income update, plus rising USDG deposits on Morpho, would show the network keeps gaining users.
  • Bitcoin's direction: If bitcoin steadies, selling pressure on altcoins like ARB could ease.
  • A close above $0.17: A daily close past that level would signal buyers have returned with real conviction.

title: Cathie Wood’s ARK Sells $85 Million In Nvidia While Buying $40 Million In Crypto Stocks — What’s Behind The Shift?
description: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has made a striking portfolio adjustment, selling approximately $84.8 million in Nvidia shares while purchasing nearly $40 million in cryptocurrency-related stocks. The transactions come as Bitcoin ETFs face renewed market pressure, raising an important question: are institutional investors beginning to identify opportunities in crypto-related businesses despite the broader market downturn? According […]
fullContent:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has made a striking portfolio adjustment, selling approximately $84.8 million in Nvidia shares while purchasing nearly $40 million in cryptocurrency-related stocks. The transactions come as Bitcoin ETFs face renewed market pressure, raising an important question: are institutional investors beginning to identify opportunities in crypto-related businesses despite the broader market downturn?

According to ARK’s November 16 trading disclosures, the investment firm sold 543,092 Nvidia shares across its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW).

Using Nvidia’s closing share price of $156.14, the transaction was valued at approximately $84.8 million. The actual proceeds could differ because the trade disclosures report share quantities rather than execution prices.

Meanwhile, ARK increased its exposure to several companies operating within the cryptocurrency and digital payments industries.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Makes A $40 Million Crypto Stock Bet

ARK’s purchases included 277,523 shares of Block, the financial technology company associated with Jack Dorsey and Bitcoin-focused payment products.

Those shares represented an estimated $23 million investment, making Block the largest crypto-related equity purchase disclosed for the session.

The firm also acquired 180,534 shares of stablecoin issuer Circle, worth approximately $10.4 million, alongside 53,760 shares of Coinbase, valued at around $6.4 million.

Combined, the purchases totaled approximately $39.9 million.

Interestingly, all three companies experienced share-price declines during the trading session. Block fell 1.92%, Circle declined 7.29%, and Coinbase dropped 6.11%.

Rather than waiting for prices to recover, ARK increased selected positions while market sentiment remained weak.

However, these transactions involved publicly traded companies, not direct purchases of Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies.

Why Did ARK Sell Nvidia While Buying Crypto Companies?

The timing is particularly interesting because Nvidia has become one of the most recognizable companies associated with artificial intelligence infrastructure.

ARK’s decision to reduce its Nvidia exposure while increasing selected cryptocurrency-related positions may suggest an effort to rebalance exposure across different technology sectors.

However, interpreting the move as a complete departure from artificial intelligence would be misleading.

ARK had purchased additional Nvidia shares earlier in November and continued to maintain a substantial position after the latest sale.

The investment manager also acquired approximately $52 million worth of SpaceX shares during the same trading session.

Furthermore, ARK reduced its holdings in Bullish and sold units of Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds.

These transactions suggest a more selective investment approach rather than an unrestricted shift into cryptocurrency assets.

ARK’s own research provides another perspective. In its November 17 newsletter, the firm described Block as an AI company, highlighting the increasingly blurred boundaries between financial technology and artificial intelligence.

What Could This Mean For Bitcoin And Institutional Adoption?

Although ARK’s purchases do not represent direct Bitcoin demand, they demonstrate continued institutional interest in businesses connected to digital assets.

Block’s involvement in Bitcoin payments, Circle’s stablecoin infrastructure, and the expansion of regulated cryptocurrency investment products all contribute to the broader digital asset economy.

This comes as BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF activity continues to attract attention from institutional investors.

The distinction between investing in cryptocurrency directly and purchasing shares in companies supporting the industry remains important.

A crypto-related stock may respond to company earnings, regulation, equity-market conditions, and investor sentiment differently from Bitcoin itself.

Nevertheless, investment in financial infrastructure could support the industry’s long-term development by expanding payment services, custody capabilities, and access to digital assets.

fullContent:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has made a striking portfolio adjustment, selling approximately $84.8 million in Nvidia shares while purchasing nearly $40 million in cryptocurrency-related stocks. The transactions come as Bitcoin ETFs face renewed market pressure, raising an important question: are institutional investors beginning to identify opportunities in crypto-related businesses despite the broader market downturn?

According to ARK’s November 16 trading disclosures, the investment firm sold 543,092 Nvidia shares across its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW).

Using Nvidia’s closing share price of $156.14, the transaction was valued at approximately $84.8 million. The actual proceeds could differ because the trade disclosures report share quantities rather than execution prices.

Meanwhile, ARK increased its exposure to several companies operating within the cryptocurrency and digital payments industries.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Makes A $40 Million Crypto Stock Bet

ARK’s purchases included 277,523 shares of Block, the financial technology company associated with Jack Dorsey and Bitcoin-focused payment products.

Those shares represented an estimated $23 million investment, making Block the largest crypto-related equity purchase disclosed for the session.

The firm also acquired 180,534 shares of stablecoin issuer Circle, worth approximately $10.4 million, alongside 53,760 shares of Coinbase, valued at around $6.4 million.

Combined, the purchases totaled approximately $39.9 million.

Interestingly, all three companies experienced share-price declines during the trading session. Block fell 1.92%, Circle declined 7.29%, and Coinbase dropped 6.11%.

Rather than waiting for prices to recover, ARK increased selected positions while market sentiment remained weak.

However, these transactions involved publicly traded companies, not direct purchases of Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies.

ARK’s decision to reduce its Nvidia exposure while increasing selected cryptocurrency-related positions may suggest an effort to rebalance exposure across different technology sectors.

ARK had purchased additional Nvidia shares earlier in November and continued to maintain a substantial position after the latest sale.

The investment manager also acquired approximately $52 million worth of SpaceX shares during the same trading session.

Furthermore, ARK reduced its holdings in Bullish and sold units of Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds.
